Sports.title: Tuchel convinced England have buried World Cup woes with Croatia thrashing
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel said England have moved on from their World Cup pain after seeing his side deliver a statement performance in Rijeka and hand Croatia their biggest ever defeat.

Tuchel was delighted after his front four combined to devastating effect at Stadion HNK Rijeka, where 6,200 local schoolchildren were allowed in free of charge even though the game was supposed to take place behind closed doors after Croatia were punished by Uefa for racist and discriminatory fan behaviour last year.

England, who have a firm grip on second place in their Nations League group and are confident of reaching next year’s finals, saw Harry Kane and Bukayo Saka each score twice and Jude Bellingham become the first midfielder to register four goal involvements in a game since David Platt against San Marino in 1993.

Anthony Gordon and Morgan Rogers were also on the scoresheet and Tuchel believes his players have used this extended international break to consign their limp World Cup semi-final defeat to Argentina to the past.

“If you feel pain you have to lay with the pain,” the manager said. “The same with disappointment. It was not easy at the beginning of the camp. We had an excellent performance against Spain. The focus in the meetings, the translation of the meetings on the pitch, to bring it within these circumstances in Croatia, to win this dominant performance is the way to move on. We’ll always have a scar, feel pain, but this is the way to move forward. We’ve played in the same manner all three matches.”

Tuchel called it a complete performance. England pressed hard, offered invention in possession and were rapid on the counterattack. Kane, who will equal Peter Shilton’s record of 125 caps when England host Czechia in their and fourth final game of the camp on Tuesday, felt it had the power and physicality of a Premier League performance.

“They just want to play like this, it’s their belief and wish, their conviction,” Tuchel said. “We don’t have to convince them. Harry plays a very intense game at Bayern. We still think we have a certain edge if we play on the front foot. If we push as often as possible in man for man it’s what the team likes. We have to manage these risks.”

View image in fullscreen England’s Alex Scott (left) said it was a ‘great honour’ to share the field with Croatia’s Luka Modric (right), one of the Bournemouth midfielder’s favourite players as a child. Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PA

There was also an impressive performance from Alex Scott, who made his full debut in midfield. “First start and what a start,” Tuchel said of the 23-year-old. “He is so smooth on the ball, his decision making. He plays with so much confidence. He is so active. The work rate off the ball makes him the complete package. We had a lot of variety in the centre of the pitch.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Scott was buzzing about facing Luka Modric, who struggled for Croatia. “It’s pretty surreal,” the Bournemouth midfielder said. “Probably one of my favourite players growing up because I had seen him as a boy. One of the best players in the world on his day. To be on the pitch with him and competing is a great honour and thankfully we got the win today.”

Kane, who is up to 89 international goals, was delighted with England’s attitude. Croatia, 13th in the world, were looking to bounce back after losing 4-1 to Spain on Tuesday.

“Every man was at the highest level,” the captain said. “They rested a lot of players on Tuesday. I feel they saw this as their best opportunity to get into those top two spots. During the week it was beautiful weather, an amazing hotel, looking out to the ocean. We could have fallen into that holiday mode.”

Sports.title: Lamine Yamal stars again as Spain see off Czechia and maintain perfect start
Sports.content:
Lamine Yamal says he feels like Superman or Spider-Man sometimes, and Spain’s fans are starting to wonder if he just might be. There is something comic book hero about what the teenager is doing right now, some unexplained super power swelling inside him. For the third consecutive game he scored inside six minutes, curling in another outrageous goal as Spain completed their World Cup homecoming in Oviedo with a 3-1 win over Czechia that leaves them a single point from the Nations League quarter finals already. Spain’s manager, Luis de la Fuente, put it simply: “Lamine Yamal is on course to become a legend.”

And yet in a game which seemed to have been done at half-time, when Spain led 2-0 after Rodrigo Hernandez had added the second and Lamine Yamal was withdrawn, his show seemingly over, the danger returned. Czechia, vastly improved after the break, pulled one back through Jiri Slama on 69 and then were denied a 79th-minute equaliser when Vassilis Fotias, the referee, who rescued Spain, harshly ruled out a Ryan Naderi goal – apparently for a foul on Robin Le Normand as the free-kick that led to it was swung in.

Reduced to 10 men soon after, still furious, Czechia finally fell with two minutes left when Mikel Merino made Spain safe. The seleccion’s first visit to the Carlos Tartiere in 11 years had ended the way they had hoped. Welcomed back as world and European champions once more, they were applauded off as winners again. A night that had begun with Rodri being presented with the World Cup by Santi Cazorla and Juan Mata, academy products at Real Oviedo and members of the generation to which all others would forever be compared, ended with a jeopardy no one anticipated when it started in a way that has become implausibly, absurdly familiar.

Lamine Yamal had scored after 104 seconds at Wembley and 70 in Seville, as Spain defeated England and Croatia. And the silly thing was that here, his goal might have come even sooner. Fifteen seconds in, the first frisson of excitement went round this place as he chased down the goalkeeper and after just fifty-seven Oviedo almost exploded. But, running on to a Dani Olmo pass, Lamine Yamal calmly guided a shot past the goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky … and past the post.

He would just have to wait until the sixth minute was up instead. Playing a quick one-two with Dani Olmo, Lamine Yamal took possession on the top right corner of the area and curled another outrageous shot into the far corner, the ridiculous becoming routine. They had been playing five minutes 20 seconds, another stadium letting out a roar that spoke of delight but also a kind of disbelief. 320 seconds he had been out there, taking him to 494 seconds to score three.

View image in fullscreen Rodri reacts after scoring Spain’s second in Oviedo Photograph: Petr David Josek/AP

Spain weren’t hurrying but they were controlling, and the chances were accumulating: by half-time they had taken 13 shots to one, and enjoyed 70% of possession. They had also added a second on 32 minutes. Rodri collected near the centre circle and did something he rarely does. The man who sometimes seems to be walking, effortlessly controlling the game with his mind and without fuss, happy enough to drop the ball off to others to do their thing, went off on a run. Advancing through the midfield, he slotted to Pedri whose return, with the help of a defender’s touch, set him up to shoot high into the net.

Next Lamine Yamal slipped in Alex Baena, denied by Kinsky. A little dinked pass from Baena then found Lamine whose shot, slightly scuffed, went wide. At the break Baena, who had drawn “oohs” with one glorious touch, was withdrawn and so too was Lamine Yamal, his work here done, another show over. The game, on the other hand, was not. That at least was Czechia’s intention and it should probably have been their reward too, the visitors taking a decisive step forward and a degree of control. They also reduced the deficit with 20 minutes to go.

The move began deep: as it progressed up the right and through the middle, Jiri Slama was sprinting to catch up. Adam Hlozek saw him coming and played the ball into his path for him to steer it low and true beyond David Raya.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

A first error from Spain’s keeper almost gave Czechia an equaliser when Raya stepped out to play and his misplaced pass only found Ondrej Lingr, and a second error really should have done soon after. But if there was relief for Spain when Lingr’s shot drifted wide of an unguarded goal, it was even greater when the referee ruled out Ryan Nadel’s effort.

For Czechia there was disbelief. Michal Sadilek’s long cross had been headed goalwards by Ladislav Krejci, and Raya, reaching by the bar, could not hold on. The ball dropped on the line, where Nadel nudged it in. The referee, though, had blown. For Santi Denia on the touchline it was hard to take and it was equally difficult not to feel sympathy. All the more when Krejci was soon sent off and then Víctor Muñoz was sent clear, dashed into the area where Kinsky blocked and Merino, forever alive, finished off the festivities.

Sports.title: Bowie gets Pocognoli off mark with Scotland victory in North Macedonia
Sports.content:
This was an occasion on which Scotland dare not stumble. By the time Kieron Bowie smashed home a seventh minute opener against a North Macedonia side not without its troubles to seek, it was already clear they would not. Bowie afforded Sébastien Pocognoli his first goal as the Scotland manager. Later, the Belgian had his maiden victory confirmed. Anything else, against such a dismal level of opposition, would have been worthy of significant Scottish embarrassment.

John McGinn’s 22nd goal for his country, coming from the penalty spot, meant the scoreline at least almost reflected Scotland’s dominance. Only Scott McKenna’s late sending off and a failure to notch three, four or five could have irked Pocognoli. Scotland remain alive and kicking in section B1 of the Nations League while aware they will face far, far stiffer challenges. Scotland needed to be professional in North Macedonia and met that task appropriately.

On the occasion of Andy Robertson’s 100th cap, it appeared in the early stages that the Tottenham full-back had been stung by criticism of recent performances in Scotland colours. Robertson marauded forward at will, including inside five minutes where he forced Stole Dimitrievski into a fine save. McGinn, like Robertson, has been the subject of some scathing words. McGinn’s response was as forceful as his teammate.

It was Bowie, though, who afforded Scotland crucial early leeway. Jack Hendry’s red card in the early stages of Tuesday’s loss to Switzerland led to Bowie being withdrawn from the Scotland attack. Pocognoli retained faith in Bowie in Skopje. Bowie had plenty to do when collecting Billy Gilmour’s pass, 25 yards from goal and with two defenders in close proximity. He set himself before firing a terrific left-foot shot beyond the helpless Dimitrievski.

McGinn’s outrageous pass from the right-back position to Robertson, who was operating as a left winger, should have ensured a Scotland second. Robertson opted to shoot and dragged his shot wide when a square pass to Oli McBurnie was the more sensible option. As Ben Gannon-Doak and Bowie missed opportunities, North Macedonia opted for two substitutions with just half an hour played.

View image in fullscreen Kieron Bowie fires Scotland ahead during the first half. Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PA

Scotland’s lack of ruthlessness was their only concern. Gannon-Doak was clean through on Dimitrievski within five minutes of the restart but shot tamely at the goalkeeper. Gannon-Doak and Scotland soon believed they had won a penalty, only for the video assistant referee to rightly highlight the Bournemouth player had stood on the foot of Matej Gashtarov rather than vice versa. North Macedonia were clinging on as Bowie tested Dimitrievski from close range.

Officialdom was soon to smile on Scotland. The match referee had originally given a foul against McKenna as the centre-back nodded the ball down towards Bowie from a Scotland corner. Not only was that decision reversed but Bojan Miovski was penalised for blocking Bowie’s shot with an arm. McGinn finished low and hard to close this game as a contest. Only three players have scored more Scotland goals than the Aston Villa midfielder.

Ryan Christie’s arrival at half-time added composure and creativity to the Scotland midfield. He looks the ideal candidate to link play in Pocognoli’s final third. It will be a surprise if Christie does not start when Slovenia visit Glasgow on Tuesday. Angus Gunn, whose position as the Scotland goalkeeper was questioned before this game, had nothing whatsoever of consequence to do.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

McKenna will miss Slovenia’s visit after upending Agon Elezi, six minutes from time. The episode was regarded as the denial of an obvious scoring opportunity. Robertson’s slack pass had landed his teammate in bother.

Robertson later admitted he owes McKenna an apology before reflecting on his cap milestone. “It means everything to me and my family,” said the 32-year-old. “It has been an unbelievable journey. It is emotional for me because I love this country and this is a special achievement. I believe I still have a lot to give.”

Handily for Pocognoli, Scotland did not need 11 men to win. McGinn was denied his second of the evening in stoppage time. North Macedonia, who have now gone seven games without scoring a goal, are a desperate lot.

Sports.title: Let there be blanks instead of Manchester City’s name on trophies: there was no honour there | Jonathan Wilson
Sports.content:
At half-time in the 2014 League Cup final, Sunderland led Manchester City 1-0. Yaya Touré equalised with a casually brilliant 30-yard clip 10 minutes after the break, and City went on to win 3-1. City, we now know from the independent commission, were at the time involved in a prolonged and calculated act of cheating, while Touré, the leaks in Der Spiegel suggested, was being paid via a dual contract to disguise exactly how much City were spending. Although precise details were left to the appendices, the commission’s report refers to payments “not recorded in an employment contract … but instead recorded in a consultancy agreement”.

Had Sunderland won, they would not merely have ended a 41-year wait for a trophy but would have qualified for the following season’s Europa League. It’s possible, of course, that the strain the extra games placed on the squad would have led to relegation in 2015, rather than the familiar trope of sacking a manager, in this case Gus Poyet, midway through the season, and surviving thanks to a bump under his successor, Dick Advocaat.

But it’s also possible that the greater exposure brought by European football, the surge of positivity engendered by unfamiliar and unexpected silverware, may have led to Premier League consolidation, stability and semi-regular European qualification.

Should Sunderland feel cheated? Of course they should, just as those who came second behind Lance Armstrong should feel cheated; just as Liverpool and Arsenal should feel cheated over the League Cup finals of 2016 and 2018; just as Stoke should feel cheated over the 2011 FA Cup final; just as Manchester United should feel cheated over the Premier League titles in 2012 and 2018 and Liverpool should in 2014; just as every club who played in the same competitions as City between 2009 and 2018 should feel cheated. But does that mean the 2014 League Cup should be taken from City and awarded to Sunderland?

These are two different questions, and it’s probably best to deal with the latter first – and this, unfortunately, is where subjectivity is unavoidable. I can’t speak for other Sunderland fans but, personally, I wouldn’t want it.

Perhaps this comes from never having seen my club win a major trophy. If it happens, I want it to be pure. I want images that will be remembered down the generations, like the highlights of 1973 – Ian Porterfield’s goal, Jim Montgomery’s save and Bob Stokoe’s celebratory skip across the pitch in mac and trilby.

I want the surge of adrenaline when a goal is scored, the agonised wait of injury time, the rush of the final whistle. I want tears and hugs and community and togetherness, all the things my dad’s generation banged on about. I want to get drunk and sing on a train. I don’t want to find out via an alert on my phone 12 years after the fact as I unpack the dishwasher.

View image in fullscreen Manchester City’s Yaya Touré equalises against Sunderland in the 2014 League Cup final. Photograph: Eddie Keogh/Reuters

Others may feel differently but the arithmetic of trophies won seems far less important than the experience of winning and the memories and sense of comradeship it provokes. Glory denied cannot be rectified a generation later by an independent commission, no matter how august.

Awarding rivals league titles seems even less satisfactory. In the 2017-18 season, for instance, the league was effectively over by the end of January with City 15 points clear.

As City went on to amass 100 points, there was little point in the four sides behind them – Manchester United, Liverpool, Chelsea and Tottenham, who were separated by five points – exerting themselves to try to rein City in.

Their priorities changed. United, Chelsea and Spurs all reached the FA Cup semi-finals. Liverpool got to the Champions League final. In those circumstances, why would any of them have prioritised the league? To award United, who finished second, the title, would seem not just empty but arbitrary.

That, though, does not mean City should not be stripped of those titles. They won them unfairly; why on earth should they be allowed to keep them? (And yes, something similar could be said of Chelsea, but that’s an argument for why Chelsea should also have been stripped of titles, not for why City should not be).

How can those trophies be left in the record books for future generations unquestioningly to see? How can City stand as the fourth-most successful side in league history when so much of that success was achieved by cheating?

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The argument will be made that City’s players strived hard for those trophies. But so did players for those other teams, the ones who weren’t cheating. And how much easier to win in a deep squad full of high-grade players, drawn to City by the money they were offering, money whose source, the independent commission concluded, had been disguised in contravention of Premier League regulations.

View image in fullscreen Manchester City with the League Cup in 2014, one of seven major trophies won between 2009 and 2018. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

Euphoric memories cannot be expunged, but it is for City fans (and players and coaching staff and directors) to decide what to do with them. If they still want to exult in Sergio Agüero’s 94th-minute winner to claim the 2012 Premier League title, nobody can stop them. But the rest of the world knows what it was based on, that as the rest of the Premier League played to regulations voted in by the clubs themselves, City did not.

That would mean that there was no Premier League champion in 2012, 2014 or 2018, no FA Cup winner in 2011 and no League Cup winner in 2014, 2016 or 2018 (and it does not seem unreasonable to wonder, when all this is done, whether there might be more to be investigated after 2018). If there are blanks on the roll of honour, let them be; there was no honour there.

Let the spaces stand as testimony to what those seasons were. Let them stand as a memorial to the years when a foreign entity tried to subvert English football, when a foreign entity took this country’s greatest cultural mode, and all the passion and all the feeling, all the sorrow and all the joy, all the love it has entailed, and tried to twist it for its own political ends. Let them stand as a warning of the dangers of laissez-faire capitalism, when everything, no matter how beloved, could be sold off to the highest bidder.

And let them stand as a monument to a Premier League that finally – belatedly? – took action, to a process that maintained its independence, to an institution that, at no little risk to its own wellbeing – a risk that has not gone away – in the end preferred justice and fairness and decency over grubby deals with the rich and powerful.

Let the years without a champion stand for ever vacant, both as a rebuke and as a tribute. Sometimes, emptiness can be the most eloquent statement of all.

Sports.title: Ireland cut short news conference as mood darkens further before Israel game
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland’s press conference on the eve of their second Nations League match against Israel in Serbia was cut short as the head coach, Heimir Hallgrímsson, fielded questions from Israeli journalists.

Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in Hungary in their first match on Tuesday after a turbulent buildup in which the Irish squad voted to fulfil the fixture despite unease among the team over the war in Gaza.

During that match the Irish players wore armbands and pointedly lowered their heads while the Israeli national anthem played. There were no handshakes between the captains before kick-off.

With the return leg taking place on Sunday in Backa Topola after the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) refused to host the match at home for security reasons, it was the Ireland manager’s pre-match press conference on Saturday that gave rise to new tensions. One reporter questioned Hallgrímsson on his thoughts about the incident on Wednesday during a Flydubai flight from the UAE to Israel.

“What do you say about the people that you support? Their ideology is based on murder,” the journalist asked. “Just this week, one of them tried to kill 170 Israeli passengers, including 27 innocent children and thousands of others.” An Irish press officer replied: “We are not doing any questions like this today. We are doing football questions.”

Another journalist then addressed the Ireland manager: “Your players call our players monkeys during the match …”, only to be immediately interrupted by an FAI official repeatedly insisting “that is completely untrue”, while the microphone was taken away from the reporter.

View image in fullscreen Republic of Ireland players bow their heads and wear black armbands in recognition of all lives lost in the Gaza conflict before facing Israel. Photograph: Bernadett Szabó/Reuters

“Don’t touch me, don’t touch me,” the journalist exclaimed, as the Irish delegation brought the press conference to an abrupt end.

Hallgrímsson had earlier been asked if there should be a conversation about whether Ireland and Israel should meet each other again. He responded: “That’s maybe a question that is not for me to answer. But given that we now have the possibility of looking back and seeing all the things that happened, I think Uefa must take that into consideration that they can’t have this happening again just for players’ welfare.

“And, yeah, but it raises awareness of the things that are going on. And, if it changes anything, I think that’s worth it. But I think it’s not for me to answer this one. It’s a good question to Uefa.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“Surviving this, coming out of it together as one would be a massive win for me. That is coming from my heart,” Hallgrímsson added. “All the challenges that this team has gone through, all the criticism. Just surviving as a group after this game, that would be a big win for me and for this group, for the association. There’s been a lot of emotions from the people in Ireland about this, and obviously that affects the players as well.

“We want to do good, but it’s always going to be a challenge when the environment is as noisy as it is. So we try to focus on the football side, and we’ve done a lot of things to help in that area. One change that we’ve done in the last games is before we go on to the pitch, we do a little prayer and a huddle with the players and all the staff, just to cool our heads before we go on to the pitch.

“Conor Coventry has taken that part, so he is now called Brother Coventry in the squad. But it’s really good when you go into a high-intensity and big-pressure game like we’ve been doing, to start the game with cool heads.”

Sports.title: Celtic fans throw tennis balls at club owner Dermot Desmond during golf tournament
Sports.content:
Celtic’s principal shareholder Dermot Desmond had tennis balls thrown towards him during his visit to the Alfred Dunhill Links golf tournament at St Andrews in a protest from fans.

The 76-year-old – who has been criticised by supporters for an apparent lack of progress on the pitch – was taking part in the pro-am event on Saturday when the disruption happened on the green of the 15th hole.

Tennis balls with pictures of Desmond’s face crossed out were thrown on to the green, with Desmond then escorted off the course by security.

The Celtic Fans Collective later released a statement on X, which included video and pictures of the protest, calling for change at the top of the club.

View image in fullscreen Dermot Desmond is driven away from the course after the fans’ protest. Photograph: Stuart Wallace/Shutterstock

“Dermot Desmond has essentially been allowed to run Celtic Football Club whilst using his wealth to hide from supporters and accountability,” the statement said. “Fans took the chance today to send a message that this arrangement cannot continue.”

On Saturday evening, Celtic issued a lengthy and strongly-worded statement against the “premeditated action” which “brought shame upon” the name of the club.

The statement read: “Celtic Football Club has never sought to prevent supporters from expressing criticism of the club, its board or its shareholders. Supporters are entitled to disagree with decisions, to make their views known and to protest peacefully. What occurred at St Andrews represents a significant and unacceptable escalation.

“Those responsible have brought shame upon the name of Celtic Football Club and upon a reputation which generations of Celtic supporters have spent more than a century building. The club no longer accepts that the Celtic Fans Collective can credibly claim to represent the wider Celtic support. Those responsible for today’s events certainly do not speak for the many thousands of Celtic supporters who express their views passionately, peacefully and responsibly.”

Celtic said the club would not be “intimidated or coerced by organised acts of disruption”, adding “there is a line between protest and deliberate disruption. Today that line was crossed … The club will protect its employees, directors, shareholders and supporters. The reputation of Celtic Football Club is non negotiable.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Martin O’Neill’s side – who claimed the Premiership title ahead of Hearts after a final-day decider last season as part of a domestic double – currently sit top of the table, two points clear of rivals Rangers.

Celtic, though, lost the last three games before the international break, including two defeats by Rangers, one at Parkhead, and were also beaten 3-1 at home by Ferencvaros in their opening Europa League fixture.

Sports.title: ‘Portugal’s greatest symbol’: Bruno Fernandes backs Cristiano Ronaldo despite walkout
Sports.content:
Bruno Fernandes has said Cristiano Ronaldo remains “the greatest symbol” of the Portugal team, despite his decision to walk out on the squad this week.

Ronaldo said on Wednesday he had left the team camp after the Portugal coach, Jorge Jesus, said he would not start against Denmark. Portugal went on to win the Nations League contest 4-2 without him, and Ronaldo’s international future remains in doubt.

The Manchester United midfielder Fernandes called for unity after a tumultuous few days in which Portugal fans’ opinions have been split over Ronaldo’s decision, and the future for their country’s leading goalscorer and most capped men’s player.

“Regarding Cristiano, I had a conversation with him, and what I told him, and what I repeat here, is this – the most important thing is that, regardless of what happens, Cristiano Ronaldo will never cease to be the greatest symbol of our national team, of our football, and of the country, for what he has done not only in Portugal but throughout the world,” Fernandes told reporters on Saturday.

“He has a reserved place not only among the best of all time, but also in the hearts of all Portuguese people, and the most important thing is that we stop dividing things,” Fernandes added. “There are no divisions in the national team, it is one and will remain so, despite any noise that may come from outside.

“We are outside of this controversy, but what I ask is that the country does not divide itself, does not make choices, that it respects all sides. At the same time, Cris is and will be the biggest icon of our national team, he deserves everyone’s respect, regardless of who likes him more or [who likes him] less.”

Portugal beat Norway 2-1 in Oslo last Sunday with Ronaldo an unused substitute, then prevailed 4-2 in Copenhagen after his departure from the squad, with Fernandes wearing the captain’s armband. The Nations League holders face Norway again on Sunday, this time in Porto.

Jorge Jesus, who managed Ronaldo at the Saudi side Al-Nassr before taking the national team job, said the 41-year-old was a “symbol of Portugal,” adding that there would be time to speak about him after the Norway game.

“I’m going to focus on the team, on the opponent which is Norway, one of the five best teams in Europe. That’s the problem right now,” said the 72-year-old coach.

Sports.title: Zigiotti Olme capitalises on Liverpool mistake to keep Manchester United moving up WSL
Sports.content:
Julia Zigiotti Olme’s sixth-minute lob proved enough to earn the Manchester United coach, Eva Olid, a second Women’s Super League victory of the season with a 1-0 home win over Liverpool.

Zigiotti Olme capitalised on a mistake by Liverpool goalkeeper, Khiara Keating, and, despite some late pressure by Gareth Taylor’s side, United held on to make it back-to-back league wins.

After a shaky start under the new head coach, Olid, the Spaniard has now masterminded four consecutive victories in all competitions and United are unbeaten in five matches.

This was United’s 250th match since the team reformed in 2018 and Olid watched her side mark the occasion with the breakthrough after six minutes.

It was a moment to forget for England goalkeeper Keating after her pass out from the back was intercepted by Zigiotti Olme, who composed herself and chipped home in superb fashion.

Liverpool pushed for a leveller and drew a double save from the United goalkeeper, Phallon Tullis-Joyce, midway through the first half. Cornelia Kapocs had a low effort saved by Tullis-Joyce, who got up quickly to deny Beata Olsson on the rebound as well.

United’s Jess Park hit the crossbar before half-time with a left-foot strike from the edge of the box before Keating saved at her near post from Andrea Medina on the rebound. Liverpool’s best chance of an equaliser came 20 minutes from time when Jenna Clark found herself free at a corner but she could not direct her header on target.

The win moves United level with Liverpool in the WSL, with both teams three points off the European places.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo in cryptic swipe at Portugal teammates over Lionel Messi view
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo in cryptic swipe at Portugal teammates over Lionel Messi view

Cristiano Ronaldo has liked a social media post accusing his Portugal teammates of not treating him with the same respect as Lionel Messi.

The 41-year-old is facing a potential six-month ban from international duty if he is found guilty of abandoning the national team.

2 Ronaldo's international career could be over - 23 years after making his Portugal debut Credit: AFP

Ronaldo's Portugal legacy has been called into question after he walked out of their training camp midweek.

Why did Ronaldo pull out of the national team camp?

The five-time Ballon d'Or winner made the decision in the aftermath of his side's 2-1 win away at Norway in the Nations League.

For the first time since Euro 2008, Ronaldo was an unused substitute.

He has since vowed 'to tell the truth' over his shock departure, with boss Jorge Jesus standing by his choice to leave the veteran forward on the bench.

In the aftermath of Ronaldo's exit, his iconic No.7 shirt was immediately given to Galatasaray winger Rafael Leao.

Meanwhile, Paris Saint-Germain midfielder Vitinha has declared Portugal 'took a step forward' in their attacking play after beating Denmark 4-2 - their first game without Ronaldo.

Though Manchester United skipper Bruno Fernandes has defended Ronaldo's actions, declaring he remains his country's greatest sporting icon.

What post did Ronaldo like on Instagram?

Speaking after that match, ex-Brazil international Felipe Meslo scolded Portugal's squad.

The former Juventus and Inter Milan star stated Ronaldo's long-time rival Messi was worshipped during his time at Argentina - a far cry to how the Real Madrid icon was treated.

His comments were shared by Sport TV's Instagram account, which earned a like from Ronaldo.

In the clip which has gone viral, Melo said: "I see a grotesque difference in the players’ treatment with Cristiano Ronaldo in relation to Argentina players with Messi.

"I see much more respect from the opponents who play against Cristiano Ronaldo, I think that’s wrong.

"No one reaches the level of Cristiano Ronaldo. It’s unacceptable.

"You can’t let the best player in history leave like that, as if nothing had happened. You can’t."

What did Ronaldo say in his statement?

While Ronaldo has not commented on his Portugal future - unlike his sister who has hinted he has retired from international football - he didn't hold back when taking to Instagram.

He wrote: "After the press conference of the national team, and following a conversation with the President of the Portuguese Football Federation, I have decided to leave the national team camp.

2 Ronaldo may never don the famous Portugal jersey again with the forward in danger of receiving a ban Credit: Getty

“In time, I will tell all the Portuguese the truth about the reasons that motivated me to leave the national team, to which I always devoted myself.

“Now is the time to wish Portugal and all my teammates good luck, without exception.”

Sports.title: Celtic owner ambushed and escorted out by security during golf round alongside Brooks Koepka
Sports.content:
Celtic owner ambushed and escorted out by security during golf round alongside Brooks Koepka

Celtic owner Dermot Desmond had to be escorted off Dunhill Links at St Andrews golf course on Saturday as Celtic fans launched tennis balls at him.

The 76-year-old Irish billionaire was the target of the protest while he was playing a round with five-time major winner Brooks Koepka.

3 Desmond is an unpopular figure at Celtic at the moment Credit: Getty

The incident happened on the 15th hole and the tennis balls had pictures of the owner's face on them.

Desmond completed his round of golf with the LIV Golf star before he was escorted away by security.

The Irishman was competing in the Pro-Am ahead of the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship, where his son Ross will be a contender.

And despite the disruption, the duo did finish their rounds.

Since the incident, the Celtic Fans Collective have claimed responsibility and issued a statement.

They said: “Dermot Desmond has essentially been allowed to run Celtic Football Club whilst using his wealth to hide from supporters and accountability.

“Fans took the chance today to send a message that this arrangement cannot continue.”

Desmond has been involved with Celtic since 1995 and is the largest shareholder at the club, owning between 34.6 and 34.9 per cent of the Scottish giants.

Why is Dermot Desmond being targeted?

Opposition towards Desmond is a steady build-up of frustration at the Celtic ownership from fans, rather than frustration over a poor start to the season from the SPFL champions.

The supporters want the board to match their ambitions, recruit wisely and communicate with them.

In the latest set of financial accounts, Celtic posted a loss of £4.8million, which was a startling drop from £22m profit the year before.

This led to a statement from the Celtic Fans Collective in September.

They said: "Anger at recent shambolic results on the park in big games was compounded yesterday by Celtic plc latest financial results.

"The statements from the 'interim' chairman (Brian Wilson) and CEO (Michael Nicholson) typically lacked humility and did little to improve the mood. Supporters are not fooled.

"The stark reality is that Celtic FC is underachieving across the club and the trajectory is alarming.

"We have highlighted the signs of this decline since our formation. We will continue to hold the club to account and fight for the standards that the Celtic support deserves.

3 Celtic Park isn't a happy place at the moment with fan anger growing Credit: Getty

3 Martin O'Neill is also under increasing pressure as well Credit: Getty

"Celtic Fans Collective representatives met with Celtic FC yesterday to discuss the club's fan engagement strategy. We also the took opportunity to express the deep frustration at the continued mismanagement of the club. A full update will be shared with members shortly."

The unrest can be traced further back to the summer of 2025 when Brendan Rodgers asked for more signings and didn't get them, while Adam Idah was sold to Swansea City without a replacement.

The end result was an open letter to the board and a vote of no confidence in them once they responded.

Rodgers resigned shortly after with Frenchman Wilfried Nancy arriving for a brief but shambolic spell.

This further eroded fans' confidence in the board, and despite Martin O'Neill's arrival and dramatic title win last season, the concerns remain.

Celtic fans will now hope that there is a response from the board.

Sports.title: Ex-Chelsea star forced to intervene after vicious tackle sparks on-pitch brawl
Sports.content:
Former Chelsea star and assistant manager Jody Morris was forced to jump in and defend his teammate in a huge on-pitch brawl.

Morris was representing St. Johnstone in the Tennent's Sixes on Saturday evening when things got incredibly heated.



4 A brawl broke out on the opening night of the Tennent's Sixes on Saturday following an aggressive tackle Credit: Premier Sports

Frazer Wright, who played over 100 games for St. Johnstone, smashed into Dundee's Morgaro Gomis, sparking total chaos.

Gomis had his legs completely wiped out from underneath him as he was clattered by Wright on the edge of the box.

The aggressive tackle instantly saw Gomis try and get back to his feet to confront Wright, but the latter was already coming towards him, with other players then storming towards the pair.



Wright was pushed over by a Dundee United player, falling to the ground, with Gomis being held back in the brawl.

Former Chelsea midfielder Morris then tried to intervene, pulling multiple people away from the clash, including Wright, who had plenty directing their anger his way after his challenge.



Things eventually calmed down, but the referee instantly brandished the red card for the ex-St Johnstone centre-back once he was finally separated from the chaos.

Wright then slumped off to the sin bin, sitting there for the remainder of the game at the Braehead Arena.



Fortunately for him though, St. Johnstone managed to hang on to a 2-1 win against Dundee United.

'We're a little bit old school'

Morris spoke about the incident post-match after trying his best, and seemingly failing, at breaking things up on the pitch.

He said: “I suppose it’s just two teams that want to win, isn't it?

4 Wright flew into a challenge on Gomis, clattering his opponent and taking his legs from underneath him Credit: Premier Sports

4 Players from both teams then surrounded the pair and a brawl ensued with plenty of pushing and shoving Credit: Premier Sports



“A little bit of rivalry – I recognise quite a few faces from back in the day. We just wanted to protect the lead.

“It was a strong tackle from Frazer, but I don’t think it was a red. I think he got the ball.

“It was maybe a little bit too much for today’s game, but it is what it is, isn't it? We’re still a little bit old school.

“I think when you come across most footballers, whether they’re playing golf, Monopoly, they want to win and we’re no different.”



What is the Tennent's Sixes?

The Tennent's Sixes is a six-a-side tournament that is held over two days, including all 12 Scottish Premiership clubs.

This year's edition is the first since 1993, with legends of all teams coming together to play against each other.

4 Wright was sent off by the referee on the opening night of Tennent's Sixes, after Morris did his best to break things up Credit: Premier Sports

It is being held indoors at the Braehead Arena in Renfrewshire.

The event started on Saturday, with the brawl between St. Johnstone and Dundee United coming on opening day.



The final will take place on Sunday evening, with the winning club collecting a brand-new Tennent's Sixes trophy.

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes shares Cristiano Ronaldo plea after phone call with superstar
Sports.content:
Bruno Fernandes has declared Cristiano Ronaldo remains Portugal's greatest icon - despite the striker walking out on the team.

The 41-year-old's international career could be at an end after he departed the Euro 2016 champions' training camp midweek.

3 Fernandes remains supportive of Ronaldo, as he urged Portugal fans to not be divided by his exit Credit: Getty

In last week's 2-1 win away at Norway, Ronaldo was an unused substitute.

It was the first time in 18 years that the veteran forward had been left on the bench for Portugal.

Ronaldo subsequently issued a bombshell statement on social media to announce his exit - vowing to 'tell the truth' regarding his decision.

Portuguese journalist Pedro Sepulveda told talkSPORT in the aftermath that the five-time Ballon d'Or winner had been lied to about his game time by boss Jorge Jesus.

While many fans have been left hurt and disappointed by Ronaldo's shock exit, Fernandes has come to his defence - hailing him for what he has achieved for Portugal.

The world's most capped international player with 234 outings and top scorer with 146 goals, Ronaldo helped his side win the European Championship and two Nations League titles.

Insisting that Ronaldo has not tarnished his legacy, Fernandes, who also played with the ex-Sporting Lisbon man at Manchester United, has implored supporters to not be divided by the news.

What has Bruno Fernandes said about Ronaldo?

Revealing he is still in direct communication with Ronaldo ahead of Sunday's return meeting with Norway, Fernandes said: "Regarding Cristiano, I had a conversation with him.

"What I told him, and what I repeat here, is regardless of what happens, Cristiano Ronaldo will never cease to be the greatest symbol of our national team, of our football, and of the country, for what he has done not only in Portugal but throughout the world.

"He has a reserved place not only among the best of all time, but also in the hearts of all Portuguese people, and the most important thing is that we stop dividing things.

3 Ronaldo, who is four goals shy of 150 international goals, could be banned over decision to walk out Credit: Getty

"There are no divisions in the national team. It is one and will remain so, despite any noise that may come from outside.

"We are outside of this controversy, but what I ask is that the country does not divide itself, does not make choices, that it respects all sides.

"Cris is and will be the biggest icon of our national team, he deserves everyone's respect, regardless of who likes him more or [who likes him] less."

Fernanded also remarked: "Matters must be resolved internally and conclude well for both parties."

Could Ronaldo ever play for Portugal again?

It now remains to be seen whether the Real Madrid and Manchester United will ever play for Portugal again.

He faces a possible six-month banishment by the Portuguese Football Federation if he is found guilty of abandoning the national team.

3 The last time Ronaldo was an unused sub for Portugal came at Euro 2008 Credit: AFP

And with his contract to expire at Al Nassr at the end of the 2026/27 season, Ronaldo could decide to call time on his glittering career upon the expiration of his deal.

How have Portugal fared in the Nations League?

Portugal have won all three of their opening matches, and remain on course to reach the Finals in 2027.

Jesus' side are the defending champions having triumphed over Spain in the final in 2025 under Roberto Martinez's tutelage - which saw Ronaldo get on the score sheet.

They also won the inaugural competition in 2019 - beating the Netherlands 1-0.

Sports.title: Dele Alli trains at non-league club after building fitness at Barnet
Sports.content:
Dele Alli was pictured training with semi-professional side Windsor & Eton as he prepares to return to football.

The ex-Tottenham star remains on the lookout for the next chapter of his career having spent over 12 months without a club.



2 Alli was last on the books at Como - featuring just once for the Italian outfit Credit: Getty

Alli has been without formal employment since September 2025 after having his contract terminated at Como.

Lasting just eight months of his 18-month contract, the 30-year-old featured in just one match for the Italian side.

And that proved to be a nightmare outing having been sent off against AC Milan just minutes after coming off the bench.



Alli, who won the PFA Young Player of the Year award twice at White Hart Lane, struggled for consistency at Everton after leaving Tottenham in 2022. He then flattered to deceive during his loan spell at Besiktas.

Who has Dele Alli trained at?

Keen to maintain his fitness, Alli trained back at Tottenham in the second half of last season in the hope of finding a new club in the summer.



A transfer failed to materialise, with Alli since using the training facilities at League Two outfit Barnet.

And he has now been pictured training with Windsor & Eton, who ply their trade in Division One of the Isthmian League South Central Division.



The Royalists currently sit 12th in table after seven matches played in the eighth-tier of the English football pyramid.

While there is no suggestion that Alli will officially link up with the Berkshire club, he was all smiles when posing for a picture on the pitch at Stag Meadow.

Sharing the photo on X, Windsor & Eton said: "It was great to have @dele_official using the pitch for the day, hope to see him back at the top soon!”

Who could Dele Alli join next?

A move to the Championship had been mooted for Alli, who scored three goals from 37 England matches between 2015 to 2019.



West Ham were tipped to be a potential destination for the midfielder amid unconfirmed reports that the player had been training with the east Londoners during the summer.

It remains to be seen whether Alli would entertain a switch to Barnet having spent time with team, with boss Dean Brennan insisting he would love to have him as part of his squad.

He told talkSPORT: "I’ll take him all day long, you would be mad not to take him.

"He’s a serious footballer and look, he’s going through a real tough time.



2 Alli has rented out the training facilities at Barnet to maintain his fitness Credit: TIKTOK

"There’s obviously some kind of issue why people haven’t taken him on.

"If I do a Harry Redknapp and pull him back in, like (Paolo) Di Canio, no issue whatsoever, everyone deserves a second chance in life.

"At our football club we have lots of lads that train with us that are out of contract and if Dele wants to come train with us the doors are open.



"He can use us to get fit and train with the group."

Should Alli make the move to Barnet, he would join a side competing for the League Two title, with the unbeaten Bees second in table, while having two games in hand over leaders Salford City.

Sports.title: Two England stars handed perfect 10/10 ratings as Three Lions hit SEVEN in record-equalling thumping of Croatia
Sports.content:
Two England stars handed perfect 10/10 ratings as Three Lions hit SEVEN in record-equalling thumping of Croatia

England put in their best performance under Thomas Tuchel in a ruthless 7-0 Nations League win over Croatia on Saturday.

Tuchel's side were utterly dominant from start to finish, thrashing their opponents as they continued their return to winning ways after losing their first game of the international break to Spain.



5 England completely thrashed Croatia 7-0 in their third Nations League game of the international break on Saturday evening Credit: AFP

The thousands of Croatian children in attendance in Rijeka for the unique behind-closed-doors game will be having nightmares, as their team conceded seven goals at home for the first time ever.

Harry Kane opened the scoring with a superb finish into the top corner after being slotted through by Jude Bellingham.

That goal saw Kane become just the fourth England player ever to find the net in six straight away games for his country.



Bellingham then tapped home after 20 minutes before Anthony Gordon and Bukayo Saka got in on the act, putting the Three Lions 4-0 up and cruising at half-time.

At the break, former captain Stuart Pearce labelled the performance as 'one of the best England have ever put in'.



And they carried that on going into the second half, with Kane scoring his second of the game after 53 minutes.

Saka then also got his second after pouncing on an embarrassing error before Morgan Rogers rounded the goalkeeper netted off the bench to make it seven in the final stages of the match.



talkSPORT commentator Jim Proudfoot said: "This is a performance and a result that will send shockwaves around Europe."

And Adrian Durham agreed, as England equalled the record for the highest margin of victory in the Nations League.

You can read all of Durham's Three Lions player ratings below...

5 Kane and Bellingham were handed 10/10s for their incredible performances against Croatia Credit: AFP

Two perfect 10s

Kane and Bellingham have scooped a perfect rating from Durham after their incredible showing in Rijeka on Saturday.



The captain netted his 88th and 89th England goal in the 7-0 win, but he also showed how good he is dropping deep, even being tipped to take on a whole new position in the future.

"He's someone you can just watch and admire," Durham said.

Bellingham is another player that everyone admires, and Durham is just in awe of the 23-year-old's performance, which saw him score and provide three assists.

Speaking post-match, he said: "There’s nothing not to love about Bellingham…his performance tonight, he stayed out there when others came off and carried on contributing to things for the whole game.”

He has become the first midfielder to record four goal involvements in a match for England since David Platt scored four against San Marino in February 1993.



5 Gordon has hit his best form as an England player, netting in all of his last four appearances Credit: Getty

Gordon brings something magical

Also among the goals and assists was Gordon, who made it four consecutive England appearances finding the net.

The Barcelona winger has scored in all of the Three Lions' Nations League games of this international break and he put in another superb performance against Croatia.

"He brings something magical and positive that England feed off," Durham said on talkSPORT.



"There’s energy, pace and goals with him. Absolutely brilliant."

A dream debut for 'exceptional' Scott

Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott made his full debut for England on Saturday evening, being handed his first start.

And Durham has handed him a 9/10, praising him for his impact at both ends of the pitch on such a pressured occasion.

5 Scott made his full England debut on Saturday and Durham was delighted with what he saw Credit: Getty

He said: “I think that performance was exceptional.

"He was always looking to go forward and always in the right position when defending.”



Durham also piled praise on Tuchel, albeit questioning why Dominic Calvert-Lewin didn't get any minutes in the game.

But the overall performance from England was so good that not a single player got anything less than a 9/10.

Reviewing the 7-0 thrashing at full-time, he concluded: "That’s what we want. Absolutely magnificent.

"There has been talk of the DNA, that’s it right there, that’s what we want from England.”



5 Here's how Durham rated England's incredible performance against Croatia

Sports.title: Harry Kane tipped for surprise role change to extend career by five years
Sports.content:
Harry Kane tipped for surprise role change to extend career by five years

Harry Kane will naturally become a midfielder for England in the years to come - he could become bored of scoring.

That's the view of Three Lions legend Stuart Pearce, who has waxed lyrical over the 33-year-old's passing abilities.



3 Kane brought up his 88th and 89th international goals for England away at Croatia on Saturday Credit: Getty

Kane was once again on target twice for England in their 7-0 thumping of Croatia on Saturday - a Nations League record equalling scoreline.

It took just eight minutes for the Bayern Munich striker to break the deadlock at Stadion HNK Rijeka.

Played in by Jude Bellingham, Kane touch one touch before rifling home into the roof of the net.



But despite grabbing his 88th goal for England, it was what Kane did prior to his opener that impressed Pearce.

Speaking as part of talkSPORT's commentary team, the ex-Manchester City manager believed one phase of play showed why Kane is destined to play in a deeper role in the future.



What did Stuart Pearce say about Harry Kane?

He said: "On commentary in Prague [for 2-0 win away at Czechia], I was lauding the two occasions Harry Kane dropped deep, got on the ball, turned and played great passes through the lines.

"We've just seen exactly that just then, fantastic pass.

"I don't know if in a couple of years time when he's fed up with scoring a million goals he might just play [in] holding midfield.



"Wayne Rooney finished his international career there you'll remember."

Kane has never featured in midfield for England before, while Rooney was moved back in eight of his last ten international fixtures.

3 Kane is just one game away from equalling Peter Shilton's record appearances [125] for England Credit: Getty

With England 4-0 up at half-time, thanks to further goals from Jude Bellingham, Anthony Gordon and Bukayo Saka, Pearce doubled down on his view on Kane.



He proceeded to state that the ex-Tottenham marksman could even extend his playing career by a further five years should he be deployed in the middle of the park.

Pearce remarked: "Harry Kane has shown us, 'Look I'll give it three years up front and get a load of goals.

"'And then I'm just going to drop into a deep-lying midfield role and use my game intelligence and passing range to be a quarter-back for England for the next five years.'"

Kane would then bring up his second of the match and his 89th goal for England shortly after the break - tapping home a low cross fizzed in by Elliot Anderson on the right.



Saka and Morgan Rogers added more goals to complete a perfect away performance for England.

3 Kane has started in each of England's three Nations League matches during the international break Credit: Getty

What did Kane say about playing deeper?

Later in the game, Kane was even seen covering in defence as the Three Lions worked hard to keep a clean sheet.

And he didn't rule out the prospect of playing further back than up front in the future.



Kane told talkSPORT after the game: "I can't wait to see my last-minute defending back. I'm enjoying watching those things back.

"I always joke to the boys, I'd love to play centre-back one day or holding midfielder. I had a few opportunities out there, but I feel that I'd be more than anyone.

"I like to be involved in the game. I like to play in different positions and I always feel like I can be effective, whether it's with the ball or without the ball. From my point of view, it's a really enjoyable game."

What records did Kane create against Croatia?

Kane's opener saw him become the first England player in 78 years to score in six successive away matches on the international stage.



He could now equal the record set by Tom Finney in May 1948 of scoring in seven away matches against Spain in November.

The two-time Bundesliga winner is also the first England star to score on at least ten occasions in three calendar years [11 in 2026, 16 in 2021 and 12 in 2019].

Kane will also become England's joint-record appearance maker alongside Peter Shilton [125 games] should he feature against Czechia on Tuesday night.

Sports.title: Ex-Man United midfielder Fred scorches former Old Trafford manager years after exit
Sports.content:
Ex-Man United midfielder Fred scorches former Old Trafford manager years after exit

Ex-Manchester United star Fred provided a stinging evaluation of his time working under former boss Erik ten Hag.

The Brazilian, who now plays back in his homeland with Atletico Mineiro, featured under the Dutch manager during the 2022/23 campaign.



4 Ten Hag coached 128 matches at Man United before being sacked in October 2024 Credit: Getty

Ten Hag’s stock was high upon his arrival at Old Trafford after leading his Ajax golden generation to within minutes of qualifying for the Champions League final.

He replaced legendary figure Ole Gunnar Solskjaer in the Old Trafford dugout with club chiefs opting for a true tactician.

Although Fred concedes that Ten Hag was a tactical mastermind, his conduct with the squad left a lot to be desired.



Fred's critique of Ten Hag

“He argued with everyone. He argued with me, with Cristiano [Ronaldo], with Casemiro, with [Marcus] Rashford,” Fred explained on the Charla podcast.

“He wouldn't put me in to play, sometimes it got stressful.”

Fred also claimed that 'only his Dutch players played'.

The 33-year-old continued: “(He was) a clique-ridden coach but tactically, one of the best I've ever worked with.



“He wanted the team to run, but Cristiano (was already) older. He took Cristiano out (of the starting line-up), and then there was a falling out.”

That led to one of football’s biggest stories in recent memory when Ronaldo announced his intention to leave Manchester United after the 2022 World Cup.



The five-time Ballon d’Or winner went on to give a bombshell interview to Piers Morgan criticising elements of the club while also hitting out at Ten Hag.

Ronaldo subsequently secured a money-spinning switch to Al Nassr, paving the way for a surge of players to make the switch to the Saudi Pro League.

4 Fred was hugely critical of Ten Hag, although he did praise the Dutchman's tactical knowledge Credit: Getty

4 Ten Hag and Ronaldo shared a frosty relationship during their time at Old Trafford Credit: AFP



Fred saw out his final season at Old Trafford by lifting the Carabao Cup under the tutelage of Ten Hag before signing for Turkish giants Fenerbahce.

Meanwhile, the Dutch coach struggled in his second season at Old Trafford, finishing ninth in the table and recording the club’s lowest points total in Premier League history at the time (60).

However, he helped salvage United’s season with a heroic FA Cup final win over Manchester City to secure European football.

An underwhelming start to the 2024/25 campaign saw new minority owner Jim Ratcliffe wield the axe in late October.



He was replaced by Ruben Amorim four days later but the Portuguese boss lasted just 14 months in the job.

4 Fred achieved Carabao Cup success in 2023 Credit: Getty

Michael Carrick filled in for Amorim on a temporary basis and was handed the reins permanently after leading the Red Devils back to the Champions League.

Sports.title: 'No one should hide who they are. I'm just being me and if I can make money off that, then great!' Saracens ALFIE BARBEARY, a.k.a. Captain Underpants, on being larger than life, being forced out of Bath and Brendan Venter's horrible 'fight test'
Sports.content:
'No one should hide who they are. I'm just being me and if I can make money off that, then great!' Saracens ALFIE BARBEARY, a.k.a. Captain Underpants, on being larger than life, being forced out of Bath and Brendan Venter's horrible 'fight test'

Wearing baggy tracksuit bottoms, a similarly large jumper, leather slippers and a beanie hat, Alfie Barbeary takes a seat on the balcony overlooking a pitch at Saracens’ Old Albanians training ground. His gold earring is just about visible below the headwear.

Barbeary is one of PREM Rugby’s great characters and it will be Sarries who will benefitting from his individuality now not Bath following his summer move to the capital from the west country.

As such, there is much to discuss as he sits down with Daily Mail Sport: His latest boss Brendan Venter’s temporary job title change from director of rugby to ‘wine consultant’ so as to avoid media commitments, a summer of wedding celebrations, battling the London Underground, a fresh haircut and staying true to himself.

There is, though, only one place to start, although Barbeary is not about to question the attitude of his boss to his media commitments.

‘Brendan is the wine consultant,' No 8 Barbeary says of his eccentric South African boss. 'We tried a few glasses with him in pre-season, but that’s as far as it’s gone. I will ask him (for advice) if I ever become a wine drinker. I’m more of a lager man!

'Brendan has been great. We had fitness testing in my first week here and he almost killed me! He called it “the fight test” and it was literally a case of fighting for your life. You had to run until you couldn’t run anymore.’

Alfie Barbeary is one of PREM Rugby’s great characters and it will be Sarries who will benefitting from his individuality now not Bath following his summer move

Barbeary makes his PREM Rugby debut for Saracens as they defeat Leicester in their first game of the new season last weekend

Long seen as one of English rugby’s brightest prospects since he first came through at Wasps, the 25-year-old Barbeary moved to Bath in 2022 when his boyhood team disappeared into administration. He swiftly became a cult hero in the west country due to his impressive displays and unique personality.

It was a surprise, therefore, when Bath revealed they would not extend his contract amid a need to fit their squad's large wage bill within the league’s salary cap. Bath’s loss has been Saracens’ gain.

‘I knew a few of the boys before I came here and I’m living with Phil Brantingham, who is a great cook, so that definitely made it easier settling in,’ says Barbeary, who like most of his new team’s squad, is based in St Albans.

'Everything is a lot bigger than Bath here. It’s much closer to London. I’m still trying to work out the Tube. I got most of the way home on it by myself for the first time the other day. Phil was very impressed I didn't get an Uber. That was a proud moment for me!’

Barbeary loved it at Bath. This summer, he attended six weddings of his former team-mates, going as far afield as Portugal, Cornwall and Scotland to mark milestones for Will Muir, Will Stuart and Finn Russell respectively. Barbeary, as he always does, lived for the moment before joining up with his new team for pre-season.

‘It was carnage. Will Muir, as greedy as he is, decided to have two weddings which really didn't help,’ Barbeary says. ‘The Bath lads have been asking me if I’ve been missing them. I haven’t at all because I literally spent every weekend of my summer with them! It made it a little bit easier to leave, to be honest.

‘It was definitely tough at the time, but I had so much respect and love for the club that when I was told, I was never going to throw my toys out of the pram and stop trying. I had to crack on and do my job.

'Rugby is a business. You might have an emotional connection to a club, but you’ve got to be able to see it that way too.’

When Bath won three trophies in 2025, Barbeary famously led the club’s celebrations often wearing nothing but a pair of budgie smugglers - hence the nickname 'Captain Underpants'

Barbeary in action for his first club Wasps before they collapsed into administration

When Bath won a treble of trophies in 2025, Barbeary famously led the club’s celebrations – first on a bus tour of the city and then onwards to the Glastonbury Festival and across Europe.

He did so often wearing nothing but a pair of budgie smugglers, his then frizzy haircut sticking out wildly. It only served to reinforce his status as one of the English game’s most likeable figures, earning him the nickname of ‘Captain Underpants’. Now sporting a shorter, more business-style trim, Barbeary admits it’s time for work as he looks to impress at Saracens.

‘When I got back from holiday, my hair was just burnt. It was matted, horrible,’ he says. ‘I had to shave it off. There was no going back, so now I’m just starting that vicious cycle again of regrowing it. The big hair will come back at some point.’

Barbeary has previously admitted he might not have yet fulfilled the potential that many people saw in him in his early days at Wasps. He is yet to win an England cap for example. Does he think his off-field persona has held him back on it?

‘It’s just me, being me,’ Barbeary says. ‘I can’t say what could have been if I was maybe a bit more professional or anything like that. It’s just how I am, so I’m not going to sit here and talk about what ifs.

'With the way rugby is going, no-one should really hide who they are. My personality might come out a bit more here the more my hair grows. I don’t really hold back. If I can make money off that, I'm happy to do so!'

Barbeary is represented by the Stellar Group, whose star rugby clients Henry Pollock and Russell have both signed lucrative deals with Eddie Hearn’s Matchroom Agency. ‘I haven't been in that conversation. I think they're too busy managing Finn and Pollock,’ says Barbeary, laughing. ‘It’s just those two at the moment. He (Hearn) has got his star boys and he's going with them.’

So what about the unusual choice of clothes? 'I’m a big fan of comfort,' he says. 'You won't see me wearing anything too tight. I get absolutely ripped to shreds for these slippers, but they're the most comfortable thing I own. They’re pretty much like skin on me now.

'I had to buy a new pair because at the first of Will Muir’s weddings, the Bath lads threw one of them into the sea at night. They didn’t like them and I’m terrified of the sea!'

‘Obviously, you want to play for England,’ Barbeary says. ‘I’ve just got to do my best and perform with Saracens. That’s the first step and after that, what will be will be’

'Rugby's a business. You might have an emotional connection to a club, but you’ve got to be able to see it that way too,’ Barbeary says of the decision to let him go by Bath where he had become a cult hero

And that Test cap? ‘Obviously, you want to play for England,’ Barbeary says. ‘I’ve just got to do my best and perform with Saracens. That’s the first step and after that, what will be will be.’

Has he spoken to England coach Steve Borthwick? ‘There have been bits and bobs. But there is incredible competition in the back-row. Missing out on squads is tough to take, but there are so many other quality players.’

Impressing with what is now a star-studded Saracens squad, who beat Leicester last weekend, will only serve to help Barbeary’s ambitions. He is one of three big summer arrivals, alongside Tomos Williams and George Martin.

‘When you look at what this club has done and how much talent it has, that’s what drew me here. I’m a bit selfish. I want to be at a club that’s competing in the PREM and in Europe. If you look at the squad we have now, there's no reason why we shouldn't be in that conversation,’ Barbeary, who has replaced former Wasps team-mate Tom Willis at StoneX Stadium, says.

‘I know Tom well. It’s big shoes to fill, but I’m not trying to replace him,’ Barbeary says. ‘What he did here was unbelievable and I’ve got nothing but respect for that. If I’m half as good as him, I’ll be happy. This group is in a really good spot.’

Sports.title: Pep Guardiola spotted for first time since seismic guilty verdict against Man City: Club's former boss attends Paris Fashion Week alongside his daughter after breaking silence
Sports.content:
Pep Guardiola has been spotted enjoying Paris Fashion Week, marking the first time the former Manchester City manager has been seen in public since the bombshell verdict.

It has been a turbulent week for the decorated Spanish football manager. First, there was the seismic announcement of Manchester City's guilty verdict for financial rule-breaking over a nine-year period, two years of which Guardiola was in charge.

Then the Negreira scandal reared up again in Spain, with 50,000 pages of evidence compiled by Real Madrid landing at UEFA on Thursday, accusing arch-rivals Barcelona of making illicit payments to an influential referees' chief. The allegations also cover a four-year period during which Guardiola was in charge of the Catalan side.

For Guardiola, who departed City in the summer saying he needed to rest and 'take a step back', the past few weeks have been anything but peaceful, with his glittering legacy coming under scrutiny like never before.

Victoria Beckham's fashion show certainly appeared to provide some welcome relief, then. Guardiola enjoyed the evening at the Conciergerie, located at 2 Boulevard du Palais, once a medieval royal palace and French Revolution prison, alongside his daughter Valentina on Friday night.

He looked effortlessly stylish as he leaned against a lamppost in the French capital, wearing a striped black shirt and dark trousers as he entertained frequent requests for photographs.

Guardiola enjoyed the evening at the Conciergerie, located at 2 Boulevard du Palais, once a medieval royal palace and French Revolution prison, alongside his daughter Valentina

It marked the first time Guardiola has been spotted in public since City's bombshell verdict

After leaving City in the summer, Guardiola said of his plans for the future: 'Rest. No plans to train for a while. Otherwise I would be here. I need to step back, I will not train for a while,' he said. 'Many people when I said it will be my last season said after three months you will come back. I don’t think so, I will take a while, but I have to prove to myself (that I need a rest).'

Whether he feels differently now that demands are being made for two of his three clubs to be stripped of the glittering array of titles he won remains to be seen.

In the case of City, there has been no suggestion that Guardiola was complicit in any of the financial doping.

He firmly planted his flag with his former employers earlier this week, writing on social media: 'I want every single Man City fan to know I am here; more than ever.

‘I am, always have been, always will be behind my club, my owner, my chairman, Ferran (Soriano, CEO), the players, staff, Enzo (Maresca, manager) and you, our unique supporters.

‘Let me be clear: we will get through this together. I love you all.’

The club were accused by the top flight of ‘sham’ deals during the period they became the major force in English football.

In a damning 40-page verdict, City artificially inflated sponsorship agreements and pumped money into the club from its Abu Dhabi owners via disguised payments in a bid to swerve Premier League spending rules.

The eight-times champions were found guilty of ‘all charges related to serious breaches’ of the regulations and the majority of those in relation to its failure to co-operate with the competition’s probe.

City witnesses were also accused of lying in front of the three-person panel, in an explosive verdict that sent further shockwaves through football after news of the guilty verdicts first emerged on Friday.

During press conferences across his tenure, Guardiola always said he ‘trusted’ those in charge of the club and said he would front up to them if and when they were proven

During press conferences across his tenure, Guardiola always said he ‘trusted’ those in charge of the club when quizzed on the charges and said he would front up to them if and when they were proven.

As for Barcelona, they have repeatedly denied any wrongdoing against allegations that they paid more than £7million in a series of payments over 17 years from 2001 to Jose Maria Enriquez Negreira when he was vice president of Spain's technical committee of referees.

Guardiola was head coach of Barca for four seasons in the heart of this era, from 2008 to 2012, during which he created a team generally accepted to be among the best to ever play the game.

The club claim the money was paid for scouting and technical reports provided by a company belonging to 81-year-old Negreira since the story broke in 2023.

At the time, Barcelona president Joan Laporta said: 'Let it be clear Barca have never bought referees and Barca never had the intention of buying referees, absolutely never.'

LaLiga claimed they were unable to investigate because of the time elapsed since the alleged offences were so far in the past.

UEFA did launch an investigation although it appeared to be going cold until the matter resurfaced this year as Florentino Perez ran for re-election as president of Real Madrid with promises to get to the bottom of what he called 'the biggest scandal in history'.

On Thursday, UEFA issued a statement to confirm a 'substantial amount of documents' had landed at the door of its ethics and disciplinary inspectors and will be assessed.

Sports.title: Something on your mind, Mateo? Man City star Kovacic misses OPEN GOAL in Croatia's clash with England
Sports.content:
Something on your mind, Mateo? Man City star Kovacic misses OPEN GOAL in Croatia's clash with England

Manchester City midfielder Mateo Kovacic sensationally missed an open goal while playing for Croatia against England – with fans wondering whether club issues were playing on his mind.

Kovacic, 32, has played for City since 2023, but now finds the club engulfed in a war with the Premier League that has seen them found guilty of the vast majority of their financial charges.

City are appealing the verdict, but it emerged on Friday night that one of their main defences surrounding sponsorship from Etihad could be in tatters due to the brand previously stating they are state-owned.

And those issues could have played into Kovacic's international form as he missed a golden opportunity on Saturday.

The midfielder found himself around eight yards from goal with a pretty much empty net to pass into, but sliced wide.

He had won the ball off club team-mate Elliot Anderson, rounded Jordan Pickford, and only had to roll the ball into the net – but failed.

A STUNNING miss from Mateo Kovačić 🫣



The Man City man rounds the keeper and misses an open goal. pic.twitter.com/YfPuDehwYf — ITV Football (@itvfootball) October 3, 2026

Manchster City midfielder Mateo Kovacic missed a sitter while playing for Croatia against England on Saturday

'Kovacic missed an empty net after all that work,' one fan wrote on X. 'These City players look traumatised by the 114 charges.'

Another posted: 'These City cheats are literally quivering in their boots whilst playing knowing what they all are.'

England manager Thomas Tuchel had previously admitted the Three Lions' City players are nervous about their futures.

While City stress their innocence and have appealed the decision, Tuchel admitted that Marc Guehi, Elliot Anderson and Nico O'Reilly are naturally anxious.

The trio have been inundated with calls and messages over the past week, with O'Reilly now having flown back to Manchester for treatment on an injury.

'Are they worried or are they concerned? I think that would be a very human reaction if you don't know what's going on for the club that you signed,' Tuchel said.

'They're still young. They're ambitious. They're told they are totally innocent and don't know what's going on.

'We speak about it at dinner and at a table of eight or 12 people. Of course, we speak about it at breakfast.'

Kovacic's club face a potentially significant punishment after being found guilty of financial breaches against the Premier League

Tuchel claimed that the news around City being found guilty of the vast majority of charges had represented a 'distraction' before then clarifying that the City trio had been focused in meetings and training sessions.

'It's a big topic in camp,' he added. 'We had some time off between the matches and it is a big subject. How can it not be a topic? We talk with them but only briefly.'

The German did also suggest that he would continue considering picking players in the event that they are relegated from the Premier League as a punishment, should an appeal fail.

'I would always try to pick the best team for the camp, occasion, tournament,' he said. 'I will never rule that out because they don't play in the top flight in their country. We need to look at it case by case.'

Sports.title: Why Alex Scott can rival Declan Rice and the moment that showed Man City star's mind may have been elsewhere as England strike perfect balance in 7-0 Croatia thrashing, writes JACK GAUGHAN
Sports.content:
Why Alex Scott can rival Declan Rice and the moment that showed Man City star's mind may have been elsewhere as England strike perfect balance in 7-0 Croatia thrashing, writes JACK GAUGHAN

Thomas Tuchel was back to being serenaded by the band of travelling support once Anthony Gordon had put the Nations League tie to bed with England’s third before half time.

Argentina might not be forgotten but the 100 fortunate enough to make this trip to western Croatia were imploring their manager to give them a wave.

He didn’t, they playfully jeered and England continued pouring on the pain for an embarrassed Slaven Bilic.
