World.title: Zimbabweans struggle to rebuild after fleeing xenophobia in South Africa
World.content:
Returnees face economic hardship and limited support as they try to rebuild in Zimbabwe.

Share Zimbabweans struggle to rebuild after fleeing xenophobia in South Africa on social media

Mutare, Zimbabwe – Samantha Chimbuya had built a life in South Africa after leaving Zimbabwe in 2019 in search of better opportunities.

She found work, could afford food and believed her two children had access to better education. She also had access to healthcare.

Then, she no longer felt safe.

As June 30 approached, a deadline set by anti-immigrant activists for undocumented migrants to leave South Africa, the 30-year-old packed her belongings and returned to Zimbabwe.

“It was not safe any more. They were raiding our homes, warning us to leave. It was scary,” Chimbuya told Al Jazeera.

Chimbuya was living in KwaZulu-Natal when anti-immigrant protests intensified. March and March, one of the groups behind the June 30 deadline, accused undocumented migrants of taking jobs and putting pressure on public services.

The deadline was not imposed by the South African government, which said June 30 would be a normal day and warned against intimidation and violence. But thousands of migrants left amid fears of unrest.

Some governments organised transport for citizens returning home. Chimbuya paid for her own journey to Hurungwe, in northern Zimbabwe.

By July 28, 116,670 Zimbabweans had returned from South Africa, according to Information Minister Zhemu Soda. Of those, 36,940 were assisted by the government, while 79,730 returned independently. A further 38,057 had registered for employment, Soda said.

Hard times in Zimbabwe

For Chimbuya, coming home meant confronting many of the economic difficulties that had pushed her to leave in the first place.



She has struggled to find work and now relies on family and friends for help. Her husband remains in South Africa, where she says he is also struggling.

She had hoped to receive a grant to start a small business but said she had not received one.

Reverend Useni Sibanda, executive director of the Zimbabwe Christian Alliance, said many returnees had spent years abroad and were coming home without jobs or adequate support.

Some had not invested in homes or property in Zimbabwe while they were away, he said, leaving them with little to fall back on.

“They are coming back to a country where there are no jobs and where the social support systems may not be enough to accommodate them,” Sibanda said.

The government says it is trying to help.

Local government Minister Daniel Garwe said authorities were screening and profiling returnees to identify their skills and needs. Reintegration centres were being established, while the Ministry of Primary and Secondary Schools was considering recruiting qualified teachers among those who had returned.

Garwe also said companies were being encouraged to employ skilled returnees and that vocational training and support for people wanting to start businesses were being considered.

For some, however, the skills they acquired in South Africa have offered a more immediate route to earning a living.

Rebuilding from scratch

Sidney Bunya, from Zvimba, northeast of Harare, left Zimbabwe in March 2020 because of economic hardship.

He moved first to Johannesburg, where he took various jobs, before settling in Port Elizabeth. There, a cousin introduced him to professional carpenters.

Bunya honed his skills and eventually secured large projects, specialising in roof trusses.

But in 2026, groups demanding permits began raiding his workplace. Bunya had only his passport, and employers became reluctant to hire him because of the harassment.

He bought carpentry tools, shipped them to Zimbabwe and left South Africa before the June 30 deadline.

Using his savings, he started a business at home. It now supports his family and employs five people.

“It was difficult to set up the business. But I am getting more jobs now,” Bunya said.

Motsi said churches had also partnered with local businesses to provide training in welding, carpentry and computer science.

Calls for longer-term support

Churches have been helping returnees with shelter, food and transport, but Ray Motsi, president of the Theological College of Zimbabwe, said the needs were overwhelming.

He criticised the government for not doing enough to support people returning after years abroad.



“We need a deliberate programme to reintegrate these people,” Motsi said, arguing that returnees needed more than transport home.

Rashweat Mukundu, a human rights activist in Harare, said the government should provide longer-term assistance, including small grants, agricultural inputs and machinery, to help people establish livelihoods.

The challenge, he said, was not simply getting Zimbabweans across the border but helping them remain economically secure once they arrived.

“I plan to open a grocery store, but funding is a challenge.”

World.title: Ethiopian government troops seize Tigray’s capital Mekelle
World.content:
NewsFeed Ethiopian government troops seize Tigray’s capital Mekelle

Ethiopia’s government forces say they’ve seized Mekelle from Tigray fighters after a week of intense battles. The fighting has reignited fears of a full-scale war that could draw in neighbouring countries.

World.title: Cornell president vows transparency amid outrage over fraternity rape case
World.content:
Michael Kotlikoff expresses deep sorrow over the case, calling it one of the most challenging periods for Cornell.

Cornell University’s president, Michael Kotlikoff, has called the alleged 2024 gang rape of a student at a fraternity house “deeply disturbing”, pledging greater transparency amid mounting outrage over how the school handled the case.

“My heart aches when I think of what she experienced,” Kotlikoff said in an eight-minute video message to the Cornell community on Saturday.

He characterised the past week as one of the most difficult in the university’s history and said it would weigh on the university for years to come. “It raises heartbreaking and troubling issues about sexual assault, dehumanisation and aspects of party culture, alcohol and drug use,” he said.

The woman, identified in court documents as Jane Doe, alleges she was sexually assaulted by multiple members of the Chi Phi fraternity in 2024 and has sued the university and seven former students.

Scrutiny over Cornell’s handling of the case intensified after New York Governor Kathy Hochul said newly released information had undermined her confidence in the local prosecutor, who initially declined to bring charges.

Hochul subsequently appointed state Attorney General Letitia James as special prosecutor to take over the criminal investigation, saying she would “not allow anyone to sweep this case under the rug”.

The case has also renewed scrutiny of the “voluntary intoxication loophole” in New York law that makes it difficult to prosecute sexual assaults involving victims who voluntarily consumed alcohol or drugs, even if they later became too intoxicated to consent.



Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten had cited the legal provision in defending his original decision not to pursue charges. Hochul has pledged to push for changes to it.

At a student assembly hearing on Thursday, several speakers called for Kotlikoff’s resignation.

In Saturday’s video, Kotlikoff reaffirmed his support for an independent review of the university’s handling of the case and said Cornell’s Board of Trustees would announce details next week. He also called for a “serious look at the role of fraternities and sororities in campus life”.

James’s appointment has placed the case under a prosecutor whose office has repeatedly clashed with President Donald Trump. She has separately described the case as “an active criminal investigation”.

World.title: Serbian populist leader Vucic launches campaign for prime minister
World.content:
Former Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic is seeking to extend his hold on power through a parliamentary vote.

Former Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic has launched his campaign for prime minister ahead of a pivotal election on October 25.

Thousands of supporters of the populist politician packed the largest indoor arena in Belgrade on Saturday, as Vucic pledged a “comprehensive” victory in the upcoming parliamentary vote.

The snap election, which polls suggest could be tight between Vucic’s party and a group of candidates fielded by a student-led protest movement, was called before Vucic resigned as president on September 27, cutting short his second term by more than seven months.

Dozens of buses from across Serbia clogged streets around Belgrade Arena on Saturday, as supporters arrived at the rally in the capital carrying Serbian flags and banners bearing Vucic’s picture.

The event, televised by dozens of channels across Serbia, capped a week of Vucic touring towns and villages in an apparent bid to shore up his popularity, which has been shaken after almost two years of sustained antigovernment protests.

Vucic, on the Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) ballot, has dominated Serbian politics as president or prime minister since 2014. Barred from seeking a third presidential term, he is now seeking to extend his hold on power through the parliamentary vote.

If the SNS wins a majority of seats, the parliament is expected to elect Vucic as prime minister.

Youth movement

The youth-backed movement that led the protests has demanded accountability for the November 1, 2024, train station canopy collapse that killed 16 people in the northern city of Novi Sad.



The movement’s quest for justice over the tragedy and against corruption has grown into a nationwide political force whose electoral arm, the Student List, will attempt to oust Vucic’s government.

The Student List includes university professors, teachers, experts and others from across the political spectrum. Vucic accused those behind the movement of seeking to “bring Serbia to a halt” and claimed, without providing evidence, that it is backed by unspecified foreign agents.

On Saturday, Vucic told his supporters: “Absent an intervention of some [foreign intelligence] service, we will defeat them. And they know that.”

World.title: Mamdani, Irish PM play bingo, ‘split the G’ in New York
World.content:
NewsFeed Mamdani, Irish PM play bingo, ‘split the G’ in New York

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani shared a video referencing the viral ‘Split the G’ Guinness drinking trend while riding the G train on the subway with Irish Prime Minister Micheal Martin during UN week in September. The two also played bingo at the New York Irish Center.

World.title: Brazil’s Lula and Bolsonaro close campaigns ahead of critical election
World.content:
Latest polls suggest Lula’s lead over Bolsonaro is narrowing, with neither candidate likely to win outright on Sunday.

Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro have wrapped up their election campaigns, each voicing confidence in victory ahead of Sunday’s tightly contested first-round presidential vote.

Lula, 80, closed his re-election bid on Saturday with a march through Sao Paulo, Brazil’s economic powerhouse, drawing what his campaign called a record crowd for a closing rally.

“Tomorrow, we’re going to win the elections in the first round,” he told supporters, describing Sunday’s vote as a choice between “democracy and barbarism” and promising to “defeat the far right”.

He has also framed the election as a test of Brazil’s sovereignty, warning against “meddling” by Washington.

Bolsonaro led a motorcycle caravan through towns in Sao Paulo state, echoing the campaign style of his father, before rallying later in Rio de Janeiro. “I am convinced that everything is in place for us to win this election in the first round,” he said.

The 45-year-old is the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, a close ally of US President Donald Trump. The former leader, 71, is serving a 27-year prison sentence for attempting to overturn his 2022 election loss to Lula.

The younger Bolsonaro was photographed at his rally holding a portrait of his father.

Trump has not formally endorsed Bolsonaro but has said he is watching the election “very closely”, a level of US interest that has become a flashpoint in the campaign.

Lula’s supporters have seized on it as evidence Washington is trying to meddle in the elections, while some Bolsonaro supporters, frustrated by the cost of living, say they would welcome US pressure if it helped force change at home.

Polls released on Saturday suggested Lula was still ahead but his lead was narrowing, with neither candidate likely to win outright on Sunday. Such a result would send the race to a run-off on October 25 between the two frontrunners, a contest polls suggest would also be close.



It is a far tighter race than Lula’s last victory in 2022, when he beat the elder Bolsonaro by less than two percentage points.

Meanwhile, the Bolsonaro campaign has faced scrutiny over a film-funding scandal. Flavio Bolsonaro is under investigation over financing for Dark Horse, a biopic about his father, bankrolled by a jailed banker tied to one of Brazil’s biggest financial scandals.

Brazil’s Supreme Court authorised federal police in April to investigate whether Flavio Bolsonaro made defamatory statements about Lula.

Bolsonaro has pledged to seek his father’s release from prison if elected, and has echoed his father’s unsubstantiated claims questioning the reliability of Brazil’s electronic voting system, which analysts say could be laying the groundwork to contest the result if he loses.

Beyond the presidency, Brazil’s nearly 160 million registered voters will also choose lawmakers, governors and senators on Sunday.

Right-wing candidates have gained ground in Latin America in recent months.

World.title: Air ambulance missing on flight from Bermuda to Boston
World.content:
The US coastguard says it has dispatched air and surface crews to search for the plane near Nantucket.

Share Air ambulance missing on flight from Bermuda to Boston on social media

An air ambulance has gone missing while carrying six people on a flight from Bermuda to Boston.

The US Federal Aviation Administration told the coastguard early on Saturday that it had lost contact with the plane, a Gulfstream jet, ⁠a coastguard spokesperson told the Reuters news agency by email.

The ⁠coastguard said it dispatched air and surface crews to search for the plane near Nantucket, an island community south of mainland Massachusetts.

The National Transportation Safety Board said it was gathering information about the situation on Saturday morning but had no further update to share.

The Canadian-registered air ambulance jet had four crew members and two passengers on board when it departed Bermuda’s LF Wade International airport overnight for the flight to Massachusetts, according to a statement from the Bermuda airport’s operator, Skyport.

Canada’s Minister of Transport Steven MacKinnon said in a social media post that four Canadians were on the plane.

“We are closely monitoring the situation and are working with the relevant authorities as search and rescue ‌efforts continue,” MacKinnon wrote.

The aircraft, registered to Latitude Air Ambulance, departed Bermuda at 12:41am local time (03:41 GMT), according to data from flight tracking website FlightAware.

The plane was flying at 24,000 feet (7,300 metres) for much of the flight before descending 13,000ft (3,960 metres) in about two minutes shortly before flight controllers lost contact, data showed.

Last communication

Air traffic control audio posted by LiveATC.net offered a glimpse of the flight’s final communications before it went missing.



“Roger, you said you’re coming in blind. Is that what you said?” a controller can be heard asking the pilot.

The pilot’s transmission could not be heard in the recording. The controller later confirmed the pilot was declaring an emergency just before losing contact with the plane.

The Bermuda government is in contact with US ‌authorities and families of the passengers, Bermuda Premier David Burt wrote in a statement posted on Instagram.

“We are praying that all six people will ‌be ‌found safe,” he wrote.

Latitude Air Ambulance is based in Ontario, Canada, and provides medical evacuation services. The company ⁠did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

World.title: Tennessee prison chief to resign after Christa Pike's failed execution
World.content:
The head of prisons in the US state of Tennessee is resigning after the failed execution of death row inmate Christa Pike on Wednesday.

Governor Bill Lee announced the change on Saturday, sharing the news in a joint statement with Tennessee Department of Correction Commissioner Frank Strada.

Strada said that his stepping down is "in the best interests" of the state, and called the ongoing investigation into the incident "entirely appropriate and necessary".

Pike, who was sentenced to death in 1996 for the murder of Colleen Slemmer, survived two injections and is now in critical condition at a Tennessee hospital as her lawyers seek to commute her sentence.

"Commissioner Strada has served with integrity, and I appreciate his willingness to put the interests of Tennesseans first during this difficult moment," Lee said.

Lee has ordered an independent review into Pike's attempted execution and he halted all executions in the state for the year.

Attorneys for Pike called the resignation "justified" but said "it does nothing to help Christa now".

"What happened to her Wednesday reflects a systemic failure that goes far beyond any one person," Pike's legal team wrote in a statement. "We hope the Governor's call for a full, independent review will expose the profound problems within Tennessee's entire death penalty system."

Pike is being treated at a hospital in Nashville, Tennessee, where doctors are attempting to clear the drugs used during the execution from her body, according to legal filings.

She was injected with two lethal doses of pentobarbital on Wednesday but remained alive. She was then sent to hospital in an ambulance. While receiving the two doses, "she could be heard crying, whimpering, and breathing loudly throughout the procedure", her lawyers said.

As of Thursday night, she was unconscious, intubated and on a ventilator.

The state's Department of Correction has defended the method it used, saying "the protocol does not allow for additional procedures beyond what was carried out".

Authorities have not yet said whether they will try again to execute Pike. They have also not offered an explanation for what went wrong. Her lawyers filed an emergency motion on Friday to preserve "any and all evidence" related to her failed execution.

Pike's attorneys previously warned that her medical history and anatomy - including thrombocytosis (a blood-clotting condition) and small veins - meant there was a risk she would experience "unnecessary" pain and suffering during a lethal injection.

The attempted execution went ahead after multiple failed, last-minute legal challenges by Pike's lawyers.

The US Supreme Court rejected two separate efforts to stop the lethal injection.

Tennessee's governor also denied a clemency request from Pike, the only woman on the state's death row.

Pike was 18 when she and her then-boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, beat, tortured and killed 19-year-old Slemmer in 1995.

She was sentenced to death the following year after a media frenzy around the killing in Knoxville, Tennessee.

World.title: Cornell president says university 'must do better' after frat house rape allegations
World.content:
Cornell University's president says the school "must do better" after a woman alleged she was drugged and raped by a group of men at a fraternity house.

In an eight-minute video statement released on Saturday night, Michael Kotlikoff described the allegations raised by the woman, identified as Jane Doe, as "deeply disturbing".

The alleged incident has raised questions around the culture on campus of drug and alcohol use, and the way investigations were conducted in the case, Kotlikoff said.

Jane Doe was a 20-year-old student at the university when she says seven men from its Chi Phi fraternity assaulted her for hours in an incident involving alcohol and the drug ketamine on 19 October 2024.

She said she had reported the incident two weeks after it happened to Cornell University police, which investigated, but no charges were laid.

Last month, Jane Doe filed a civil lawsuit against the Ivy League university, in which she alleged Cornell had failed to protect her or adequately punish the men involved.

Kotlikoff said Cornell was "committed to investigating" the way the case was handled, and said the school administration and community "must do better".

"We must foster a culture in which sexual assault is inexcusable and ensure our community is empowered and understands informed consent," he said.

He added that university leaders need to create an environment where victims of sexual assault "feel safe coming forward and are treated with compassion and dignity".

Kotlikoff said it is a "defining moment" in the university's history.

"We must lead the way, we owe it to Jane Doe and to survivors of assault to get this right. And we must keep each other safe," he said.

On the university's campus this week, the BBC saw growing frustration about the situation.

World.title: Flydubai co-pilot attacked captain with axe, UAE official says
World.content:
The co-pilot who attempted to take control of a Flydubai plane travelling to Israel attacked the pilot with a crash axe, the United Arab Emirates prosecutor general has said.

The flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv carrying more than 170 people plunged 17,000ft (5,200m) two and a half hours into its journey, before passengers managed to overpower the attacker and successfully take control of the plane.

Capt Smit Machchhar said he was lying on the floor injured when he realised the plane was sinking and he had to act, explaining: "I told myself to go for one last push to open the door from inside", which allowed the passengers in.

Two reserve pilots then landed the plane safely in Saudi Arabia.

A crash axe is usually kept âin the cockpit in case of emergencies.

The weapon used has been a key question for investigators, given the stringent security on such a sensitive route. Early reports from passengers on board had suggested it might have been a knife.

The UAE attorney general told state media that investigations were ongoing to determine the full circumstances and motives of the incident.

The co-pilot who launched the attack was an Omani national, according to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Multiple media outlets including Reuters, CNN and The New York Times have named him as Hamam al-Hammami. There has been no official confirmation of this.

While working at another airline, Oman Air, US media reported that Al-Hammami was removed from flight training because of concerns over his radical views, and was given another role at Oman's national airline.

He completed a three-year distance-learning course at Buckinghamshire New University in the UK and graduated with a degree in aviation management in 2023, the university said. It added he did not take any pilot training at the school.

Speaking to Fox News, Netanyahu said that after the attacker was subdued on the flight, he called out to the crew "Kill me, kill me!"

The Israeli prime minister added: "So, it's clear that he was suicidalâ¦ It looks very likely that he was going to down the plane."

He also said the attacker "underwent Islamist radical indoctrination".

The UAE's attorney general, Hamad Saif Al Shamsi, said investigations into the incident revealed that the co-pilot attempted to carry out a "terrorist act", according to the country's state news agency.

He also said investigations were under way to establish the circumstances, motives and any links related to the incident.

Machchhar, who was stabbed in the attack, was taken to a nearby hospital before being airlifted to Abu Dhabi, where he is reported to be in a stable condition.

The pilot, who is from India, was in "good health and recovering well", the Indian embassy in the UAE said on Thursday.

"I am confident that the recovery will be there and I will become fit and healthy again," Machchhar said.

World.title: Russia hits second major bridge in Ukraine's capital Kyiv
World.content:
A Russian strike has hit a second major bridge in Kyiv, Mayor Vitaliy Klitschko has said, as Moscow ramps up attacks on critical infrastructure in Ukraine's capital.

The attack on Saturday morning injured two people, and damaged the road surface and overhead trolleybus wires on the Pivnichnyi (Northern) Bridge, Klitschko said, causing traffic jams.

It comes after the Pivdennyi (Southern) Bridge was hit multiple times by Russian drones this week, with Klitschko warning that "the enemy is tearing Kyiv apart".

Russia said its drones had hit the two bridges used to transfer Ukrainian troops and military cargo. Moscow again urged foreign citizens, including diplomats, to leave Kyiv.

The two Kyiv bridges across the Dnipro River link the western and eastern parts of the capital and had not been hit before Thursday.

The Russian strikes have severed road, rail and trolleybus links across the wide river. The ongoing drone threat means restrictions on other routes, bringing traffic jams to the city's roads for a second day - though Friday's gridlock has not been repeated to the same level.

Many of the city's residents - which number about three million - rely on the metro to travel across the city every day. The fear is this new Russian tactic will result in sustained attacks which could effectively cut the city in two.

World.title: 'Anger in the streets': Tens of thousands protest in Spain over housing crisis
World.content:
Tens of thousands of people have protested across Spain calling for greater protections for tenants after the government failed to pass emergency housing legislation.

About 50 marches took place on Saturday in cities including Madrid, Valencia and Barcelona.

"There is a lot of anger in the streets," a spokesperson for the Valencia Tenants' Union said. Clashes have taken place between some protesters and police in the city.

The measures put forward by Pedro SÃ¡nchez's leftist coalition government on Friday followed public outcry over the eviction of an 87-year-old woman from her home last month after she was unable to afford a sharp rent increase.

Her eviction triggered nationwide protests across Spain with protesters demanding lower rents, an end to evictions, and a ban on investment funds - or "vulture funds" as the government has termed them - buying property.

Sanchez's defeat in Congress on Friday heightens speculation that he might call an early general election, which was not due until next summer.

His coalition government, made up of his ruling Socialist party and junior partner the Sumar alliance, does not command a majority in parliament.

World.title: G7 to release millions of barrels of oil and diesel after Trump threat
World.content:
The G7 has announced 100 million barrels of oil and diesel will be released to ease supply concerns that have caused prices to skyrocket.

It includes a "substantial release" of diesel within 20 days, with discussions around "additional diesel releases as necessary", G7 leaders said in a statement.

The group of advanced economies, including the US, said the move would begin immediately and would last for four months.

Under the measures, which come after US President Donald Trump had threatened to ban diesel exports, there will not be any "export restrictions on energy and energy products" between G7 members.

The G7 includes the US, UK, Canada, Japan, Germany, Italy and France, with the EU also represented at its meetings.

Donald Trump had warned he would ban diesel exports from the US if European countries did not agree to put more of their own stocks onto the market. That would have eased pressure on prices for US consumers ahead of November's midterm elections, but pushed up prices elsewhere.

On Friday, he said on social media: "Europe has just agreed to release a massive amount of their heavily stocked Diesel Oil. The process will begin immediately."

His Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent had argued US farmers, truckers, and businesses "should not be left carrying the burden" as prices soar.

Speaking later at the White House, Trump said an export ban on diesel was "never really on the table".

Referring to the decision by the G7 to release fuel from reserves, he added that "what Europe did was a great thing."

"Europe has a lot of diesel and they're going to be making a major world contribution - and so are we," he said.

"And we're not going to be doing the export ban, we're going to be doing what we're supposed to do."

Trump had first said he backed a diesel export ban early last week, and was still considering it on Thursday, as his administration put pressure on Europe to tap its supplies.

Diesel is used heavily by the haulage industry and in agriculture, meaning rises in the cost of the fuel feed through into essentials such as food.

World.title: Medical plane with 6 on board missing off Massachusetts coast
World.content:
US authorities are searching for six people after a medical plane bound for Boston, Massachusetts, went missing early Saturday morning.

The Federal Aviation Administration told the BBC that it lost contact with the Gulfstream G-100 plane and put out a search-and-rescue notice just after 1:00 local time (6:00 GMT).

An air and water search is underway off the coast of Nantucket, a Massachusetts island, according to the US Coast Guard's Northeast District.

The plane departed from Bermuda's L.F. Wade International Airport at 23:40 local time, according to flight data from FlightAware, and was slated to land at Boston's Logan International at 1:30 EDT (6:30 GMT).

According to the tail number released by the Coast Guard, the plane belonged to Latitude Air Ambulances, a company that provides international medical flights for patients returning home.

Among those on board were two pilots and two medical staff, both Canadian, Clarence Togeretz, director of flight operations at Latitude, told CBC News.

The crew flew to Bermuda to collect a patient and their relative, who are not Canadian, Togeretz said.

FlightAware's tracker shows the aircraft significantly dropped in altitude before its communications went dark, plummeting from around 7,300m (24,000ft) to 3,300m (11,000ft).

Radio transmissions shows trouble with communications between the air traffic controller and the pilot, the Boston Globe reported based on transmissions provided by LiveATC.net.

"You're coming in blind? Is that what you said?," the air traffic controller asked. "Are you declaring an emergency, or no?"

The pilot's response was inaudible.

"You're coming in a little weak so I didn't hear what your response was, if you were declaring an emergency or not," the air traffic controller said, according to the Globe.

The air traffic controller later confirmed the pilot had declared an emergency.

An area fire dispatcher asked emergency crews just after 1:00 EDT to prepare to meet a plane with an "electrical issue".

The dispatcher later said "the aircraft has lost radio and radar".

World.content:
In Brazilâs upcoming presidential election, President Luiz InÃ¡cio Lula da Silva is facing right-wing challenger and ally of Donald Trump, Flavio Bolsonaro, son of former President Jair Bolsonaro.

World.title: Leaders of Peter Obi’s support groups released after 24-hour detention
World.content:
The Nigeria Police Force, Akwa Ibom State Command, has released the leaders of the Obi-Kwankwaso (OK) and Obidient movements in the state after more than 24 hours in detention following a disputed Independence Day march in Uyo.

OK and Obidient movements are political groups working toward the actualisation of the presidential aspiration of the Nigeria Democratic Congress presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso.

Elijah Noah, coordinator of the OK Movement, and Ben Smith, state coordinator of the Obidient Movement, were among nine people the police arrested during the controversy surrounding the planned 1 October political procession.

Mr Noah told PREMIUM TIMES by telephone on Saturday that all nine detainees left the police station at about 6 p.m. on Friday.

The arrests followed a directive by the police command ordering political parties and groups to reschedule previously approved rallies, meetings and processions scheduled for 1 October, citing security concerns.

The command said the directive was based on intelligence suggesting that political gatherings could be exploited to cause disturbances and threaten public peace. It maintained that the directive applied generally and was not targeted at any political group.

But the organisers disputed the police’s account of the events, particularly the circumstances surrounding Mr Noah’s arrest and the dispersal of supporters.

How the dispute unfolded

Mr Noah, speaking on XL FM after his release, said he had earlier met the Commissioner of Police, Baba Azare, who expressed concern about the command’s ability to provide adequate security for the proposed march.

He said he explained that the procession was intended to be peaceful and that 1 October was deliberately chosen because of Nigeria’s Independence Day.

He said the organisers subsequently agreed to reschedule the march after discussions with the police.

Mr Noah, however, said he later learnt that some supporters had gathered at the proposed take-off point despite the postponement.

He said many who gathered for the march had only heard about the planned march and were not on the same platform where information was posted about the reschedule, hence they still came out for the procession.

Mr Noah said that on discovering that many were already at the take-off point, he went to the area to communicate the new date to the supporters.

“I know we all believe in our principal. Let’s work with a scheduled date,” he remembered telling those who gathered.

He alleged that police officers arrived shortly afterwards and fired tear gas after seeing him addressing the crowd in an OK Movement shirt.

The allegation could not be independently verified.

In its account of the incident, however, the police said eight people were arrested for allegedly engaging in acts capable of causing a breach of public peace and disregarding lawful security directives.

The command also denied that officers fired guns and tear gas during the operation. PREMIUM TIMES had earlier reported that witnesses alleged that tear gas was used to disperse supporters, while the police denied the use of firearms.

‘People were running for their lives’

Frank Okon, the media director of the proposed march, questioned the scale of the police deployment at the scene.

“Have you ever seen, if at all there was a protest, the police outnumber those who came to protest?” Mr Okon asked.

He said he was present when the incident occurred and disputed the police’s denial that tear gas was fired.

According to him, people fled the area after the police intervention.

“This is not good for democracy because the window for campaign had opened,” he said.

PREMIUM TIMES also visited the area where the incident occurred. Witnesses told the newspaper that police officers fired tear gas, forcing people to flee.

Smith’s arrest

Mr Smith was reportedly arrested after going with other supporters to seek the release of Mr Noah and other detainees.

His arrest widened the dispute, with the Obidient Movement demanding the immediate release of both coordinators and other detained members.

The movement accused the police of intimidating its members and restricting political expression, while the police maintained that its actions were prompted by security considerations and non-compliance with its directive.

The police had earlier said organisers of the march attended a meeting with the police and were advised to choose another date because of concerns over possible clashes and public safety.

‘We have never faced this before’

Samuel Duff, secretary of the OK Movement in Akwa Ibom and one of those arrested, connected the incident to the political environment in the state.

World.title: VIDEO: I killed my girlfriend, dismembered her over HIV infection – Suspect
World.content:
A 30-year-old man, Chibuike Okpara, says he killed his girlfriend, dismembered her body and hid it inside a toilet in his apartment.

PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that the police in the state arrested the suspect for killing the victim on 19 September in his apartment at Olympic Layout, One-Day Area of Enugu State.

At the time, the police simply identified the victim as Chinyere.

Full identity revealed

In a video clip posted on Friday morning, the police spokesperson in Enugu State, Daniel Ndukwe, said the deceased victim has been identified as Chinyere Ugwu.

Mr Ndukwe, a superintendent of police, said Ms Ugwu, a 27-year-old graduate of Medical Laboratory Science, recently concluded the mandatory National Youth Service Corps programme.

The spokesperson said the police have identified her parents and siblings, assuring that the suspect would be prosecuted.

‘How I killed the victim’

Speaking in the video interview, Mr Okpara confessed that he killed the victim over an argument about who infected the other with HIV.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The suspect narrated that on the night of 19 September, he told the victim that he could cure Hepatitis C, HIV and syphilis and urged her to bring her friends who might have the disease.

He claimed that immediately after his comment, the victim accused him of infecting her with HIV.

“This led into an argument that resulted in a fight between me and her. So she held a pestle and started hitting me, but I had to withdraw it from her. I hit her, which caused her to collapse,” he said.

Asked what he did to the deceased body, he responded: “I chopped off her wrist and did some cuts on the head.”

The suspect claimed he dumped the body of the deceased in the toilet because he did not know what to do at the time.

He said neighbours who later perceived an offensive odour oozing from the victim’s corpse forced their way into the apartment and saw the body.

Mr Okpara confessed that, to prevent her family from calling her phone, he damaged her mobile phone and her SIM card too.

The suspect recalled that he met her on Facebook in 2023 before he decided to relocate from Owerri in Imo State to Enugu in December 2025.

‘Drugs pushed me to kill her’

Mr Okpara claimed that he killed the victim because he was under the influence of drugs at the time.

“I wasn’t fully aware of myself at first. I was probably on some substance,” he stammered.

‘Temper justice with mercy’

Mr Okpara pleaded for mercy, stressing that the killing of the victim was not intentional.

“I have been praying to God for forgiveness. For the fact that this wasn’t actually a clear, pure, intentional act from my angle.

“And I have been pleading for the government to temper justice with mercy,” he appealed.

World.title: Why we can’t strike despite locating kidnapped NYSC members – Police
World.content:
The police in Imo State say they have identified the location where about 19 prospective National Youth Service Corps (NYSC ) members abducted in the state are being held.

The Commissioner of Police in the state, Audu Bosso, disclosed this while speaking with reporters on Saturday.

A video clip, which showed the police chief making the remarks, has been circulating on social media.

PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that gunmen abducted the prospective NYSC members at about 6:30 a.m. on Thursday along the Owerri-Onitsha Road by Umunoha in Imo State.

The prospective NYSC members were travelling from Ibadan, Oyo State, to orientation camps in Abia and Akwa Ibom states.

The police later said 10 victims were rescued at the scene following the intervention of the police and other security agencies, while the exact number of people still in captivity was being verified.

Identified location

While speaking with the reporters, Mr Bosso said the police used drones on Friday to locate the suspected camp after security operatives trailed the abductors into the bush.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The commissioner, however, said the security agencies were being cautious because intelligence indicated that the camp had been mined with Improvised Explosive Devices (IEDs).

“Any moment, we will still move into the bush. Yesterday (Friday) we were in the bush; we trailed them up to a particular location.

“But at that point in time, we couldn’t move into where the coordinates showed us where they (abductors) are, because we ran drones yesterday. And the drone actually showed us exactly their location.

“But our predicament is that with the intel we have, the camp is mined with IEDs,” he said.

The police chief said security operatives were preparing to move into the area with heavy equipment, such as bulldozers and armoured personnel carriers (APC), in an effort to rescue the victims unhurt.

“We are moving in there with high-velocity vehicles, that is, bulldozers; we’re moving in with bulldozers and APCs to see how we’re going to rescue these victims unhurt,” he stated.

No group has claimed responsibility for the abduction.

World.title: Obasanjo, Jonathan, Gowon, others pay tribute to late Aso Rock chaplain, William Okoye
World.content:
Former President Olusegun Obasanjo has described late William Okoye as a statesman of faith and fearless voice of truth.

Mr Obasanjo stated this in a tribute read by Godwin Isaac, a bishop, at the Night of Tributes for Mr Okoye, held at the National Christian Centre, Abuja, on Friday.

Mr Okoye, former general overseer of All Christians Fellowship Mission (ACFM), was also a former chaplain of the Aso Rock Villa Chapel.

Mr Obasanjo said Mr Okoye’s death had created a monumental void across the nation, recalling their close working relationship between 1999 and 2007.

He said the deceased, who served as his chaplain, provided wisdom and guidance during high-pressure situations, beyond his spiritual responsibilities.

“As my chaplain, he was a steady, fearless, and uncompromising voice of truth,” Mr Obasanjo said.

He said Mr Okoye understood that genuine gospel ministry must address the material realities confronting the people.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The former Nigerian leader recalled that the late clergyman served on the Presidential Advisory Council on Youth Affairs and represented the FCT at the National Political Reform Conference.

He also served on the Christian Pilgrims Welfare Board and held leadership positions in the Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN) and Pentecostal Fellowship of Nigeria (PFN).

Mr Obasanjo said Mr Okoye served as chairman of CAN and PFN in Abuja, while also serving as CAN National Director on National Issues.

Former President Goodluck Jonathan said he met Mr Okoye while serving as governor of Bayelsa State and worshipping at the Aso Rock Villa Chapel.

Mr Jonathan who was represented by John Opara, former executive secretary of Nigerian Pilgrims Commission (NCPC)

recalled that Mr Okoye was then deputy chaplain to Yusufu Obaje and later served as chaplain during the Jonathan presidency.

He said Mr Okoye eventually requested to leave the Villa Chapel and recommended Obioma Onwuzurumba as his successor, alongside John Oyelade, an archbishop.

“Nigeria will miss you. Your family will miss you. The church will miss you. You stood for integrity,” Mr Jonathan said.

Former Head of State, Yakubu Gowon, described Mr Okoye as a pioneer of Nigeria Prays and praised his leadership, integrity, humility and commitment.

Mr Gowon, a retired general, who was unable to attend physically because of a trip to the United Kingdom, delivered his tribute virtually.

He said Mr Okoye’s memory would remain evergreen, recalling his support for the Nigeria Prays movement since its inception in 1996.

Victor Umeh, the Anambra Central Senator, who represented the NDC presidential candidate, Peter Obi, described Mr Okoye as a brother from the same local government area in Anambra State.

Mr Umeh said Mr Okoye prayed for peace during Anambra’s political crisis and worked to promote stability in the state.

Toyin Okoye, a pastor and wife of the deceased, thanked God for her husband’s life, describing him affectionately as “Mine.”

She said Mr Okoye told doctors at the hospital that he was not afraid of death and appreciated those who prayed for and visited them.

She particularly acknowledged the General Overseer of the Redeemed Christian Church of God (RCCG), Enoch Adeboye, and other Christian leaders who supported the family during the period.

“Your life of integrity touched lives, including my own life.

“You have fought the good fight, finished the race and kept the faith,” she said.

Paul Enenche, founder of Dunamis International Gospel Centre, said Mr Okoye was passionate about Nigeria’s spiritual and physical wellbeing.

Mr Enenche said the deceased believed God would raise Christians who would contribute significantly to the transformation of Nigeria.

The President of CAN, Daniel Okoh, an archbishop, described Mr Okoye as a preacher, trainer and mentor who dedicated his life to God and humanity.

Mr Okoh quoted Psalm 116:15 and John 11:25, saying Christians did not mourn as those without hope.

Speaking on behalf of the children, Victor Okoye said, since his father’s passing, the family had heard countless stories of his compassion.

He said his father may not have left great material wealth, but left an enduring legacy of a good name, values and kindness that money cannot buy, which they would carry forward.

NAN reports that Wale Oke, the PFN national president, led prayers for the family and the church the deceased left behind.

Mr Okoye is survived by his wife, six children, and nine grandchildren, including Victor Okoye, a journalist with NAN and the entire ACFM family.

(NAN)

World.title: North-east governors raise ₦10.8 billion to form regional airline
World.content:
The North-East Governors’ Forum (NEGF) has raised ₦10.8 billion in counterpart funding to launch a regional air shuttle, as a step toward establishing the proposed “North East Airline”.

The Chairman of the Forum and Governor of Borno State, Babagana Zulum, disclosed this on Friday during the opening ceremony of the 10th meeting of the North East Governors’ Forum in Maiduguri.

Addressing member-state governors and regional leaders, Mr Zulum stated that the balance of the counterpart fund will be remitted before the end of the month to enable the immediate rollout of the flight operations.

“The establishment of the North East Air Shuttle is a significant step towards improving connectivity within the sub-region, and we look forward to the commencement of these operations soon,” Mr Zulum said.

“To this end, ₦10.8 billion has been realised as counterpart contributions from the governors of the North-east region. Insha Allah, the remaining counterpart funds shall be received before the end of this month, this year, with a view to actualising our dream of having the North East Air Shuttle.”

He urged member states—Adamawa, Bauchi, Borno, Gombe, Taraba, and Yobe—to consolidate their commitments and work in unison to ensure the smooth take-off of the regional carrier.

Oil Exploration, $1 billion poverty fund, and security gains

Beyond the regional aviation framework, Mr Zulum highlighted key federal government interventions and economic initiatives aimed at driving recovery in the conflict-affected region.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Resumption of oil exploration

The forum chairman commended President Bola Tinubu for reviving oil exploration activities at the Kolmani oilfield in Bauchi State.

He noted that the project extends beyond oil and gas investments, offering a path toward job creation, infrastructure development, and an expanded revenue base for host communities.

Mr Zulum further urged the federal government to extend exploration efforts into other prospective locations across the region, particularly the Bama, Monguno, and Lake Chad Basin areas of Borno State.

$1 billion social protection project

Highlighting social welfare interventions, Mr Zulum lauded the federal government’s $1 billion Household Prosperity and Economic Social Protection Project earmarked for the North-east.

He described the project as crucial for a region recovering from over a decade of insurgency, displacement, and humanitarian dependency.

“Our objective must now be to move deliberately from relief to recovery, and from recovery to sustainable prosperity,” he stressed.

Security improvements and non-kinetic strategies

Acknowledging measurable improvements in regional security compared to previous years, Mr Zulum attributed the progress to the sacrifices of the Nigerian armed forces, inter-state cooperation, and non-kinetic interventions.

He referenced programmes like the Safe Corridor Initiative, which facilitated the surrender and rehabilitation of repentant insurgents.

However, he warned against complacency, emphasising that security remains the prerequisite for economic transformation, healthcare delivery, and educational development.

Key regional initiatives highlighted

The governor outlined several regional development drives coordinated under the forum. They include:

10MW Solar Power per State.

The Forum reaffirmed its commitment to establishing 10-megawatt solar power plants in each of the six member states to expand clean, reliable energy access.

Livestock value chain development

Collaborating with the newly created Federal Ministry of Livestock Development, member states plan to modernise livestock systems, animal healthcare, and processing facilities.

E-mobility fleet procurement

Mr Zulum commended the North East Development Commission (NEDC) for procuring nearly 10,000 electric vehicles (EVs) and e-tricycles.

The fleet is scheduled to be officially launched by Vice President Kashim Shettima.

Harvest management

With promising agricultural outlooks across the states this season, member states were urged to establish off-taking, storage, and processing networks to prevent post-harvest losses and add value to regional produce.

Call for unified action

Concluding his address, Mr Zulum urged regional leaders to remain focused on translating policy discussions into measurable outcomes for residents across the six states.

“Our people expect results,” Mr Zulum said.

“They expect security that allows them to live peacefully, roads that connect their communities, schools that prepare their children for the future, hospitals that save lives, jobs that restore dignity, and economies that enable families to prosper.”

The 10th meeting of the North East Governors’ Forum brought together state governors, federal officials, and key regional stakeholders to deliberate on shared economic, humanitarian, and security strategies.

World.title: NLO Cup 2026: Ogunnowo reveals motivation for revamped competition
World.content:
The Nationwide League One (NLO) has introduced a revamped cup competition to address complaints from clubs over the limited number of matches in its existing league format, its Chief Operating Officer, Olushola Ogunnowo, has said.

The competition, which will feature clubs from Divisions One and Two, is scheduled to begin on 10 October, with participating teams required to pay a non-refundable registration fee of N1 million.

Mr Ogunnowo said the initiative was designed to accommodate clubs with different financial capacities while providing additional opportunities for players to compete and showcase their abilities.

Speaking in an interview with PREMIUM TIMES, he said the league had received complaints from some clubs about the number of matches available to them, prompting the need for a format that could address their concerns without imposing additional financial burdens on others.

“As a responsible public body, we have to cater for all parties,” he said.

He explained that the NLO had sought to strike a balance between clubs financially capable of playing more matches and those with limited resources.

While the league has retained its stadium-based format for Divisions One and Two, the new cup competition offers an additional option for clubs willing and able to participate in more fixtures.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“We have modelled a stadium league for Division One and Two in the Nationwide League. We now came up with another competition, a cup competition like we have across Europe, for clubs in both divisions that can afford to play,” he said.

Mr Ogunnowo said the league was encouraged by the feedback received since announcing the innovation, adding that many clubs had expressed satisfaction with the initiative.

Home-and-away format, N1m registration fee

In a circular dated 14 September, the NLO Secretariat outlined the registration requirements and operational guidelines for the remodelled competition.

According to the document signed by Mr Ogunnowo, interested clubs in Divisions One and Two must pay a non-refundable registration fee of N1 million, which the league said would cover match logistics.

Payments are to be made into the league’s designated FCMB account, with clubs required to forward evidence of payment to the secretariat for verification and registration clearance.

The competition will adopt a regional home-and-away format, allowing participating clubs to select their preferred home grounds.

Clubs facing logistical difficulties or located close to one another may share facilities, subject to approval by the NLO Secretariat, to ensure smooth fixture scheduling.

Participating teams are also required to submit their proposed home grounds ahead of the competition to facilitate zonal allocation and fixture arrangements.

NLO targets global exposure for players

Beyond providing additional matches, the league is positioning the competition as a platform for improving players’ visibility and creating opportunities for international career progression.

The NLO said all matches would be livestreamed on its official platform, enabling international scouts, club directors and foreign representatives to monitor players’ performances in real time.

The initiative will be supported by three technology partners: FutbalConnect, SofaScore and Zkyte Technologies.

FutbalConnect will facilitate connections between players and international scouts, agencies and clubs, while SofaScore will provide live scores, player statistics and performance analytics.

Zkyte Technologies will handle streaming delivery, digital infrastructure and broadcasting technology.

The league has also directed participating clubs to update their team rosters and player profiles ahead of digital media registration and broadcast profiling.

It said the digital coverage was part of its broader efforts to enhance players’ exposure, improve returns on investment for clubs and support talent development.

The NLO Cup’s introduction comes as the league seeks to expand competitive opportunities within Nigeria’s lower-tier football structure while recognising the financial realities facing participating clubs.

By maintaining its existing league format alongside the additional cup competition, the NLO is seeking to give clubs greater flexibility in determining their level of participation without making the expanded schedule compulsory for all teams.

World.title: Musa Francis, Akanbi Aderonke win 2026 Abeokuta 10km Race
World.content:
Musa Francis James and Akanbi Aderonke Olufunmilayo emerged as the men’s and women’s winners respectively at the fifth edition of the Abeokuta 10km Race in Ogun State on Saturday.

Francis James led the men’s field from the finish, completing the 10km race in 30:25.33 to claim the $1,000 first prize.

Ilya Raymond finished second in 30:38.06 to collect $750, while Gyang Sunday completed the men’s podium in 30:47.00 and received $500.

The women’s race followed a similar pattern, with Akanbi Aderonke Olufunmilayo taking the top position after finishing in 35:00.69 to win $1,000.

Bulus Mary Jah came second in 35:58.71 and received $750, while Nwantiyi Teyei Davou finished third in 36:03.09 to take home $500.

The results reflected the competitive nature of the race, which brought together athletes, fitness enthusiasts and members of the public for the fifth staging of the event in Abeokuta.

For the winners, the achievement was also a reward for their preparation and an opportunity to compete on a platform that continues to attract athletes to the city.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Francis James said he was pleased to see his preparation pay off after crossing the finish line first, while also acknowledging the platform provided by the organisers.

“I’m very happy with the victory,” James said.

“It feels good to see all the hard work and preparation pay off. I’m grateful for the opportunity to compete here, and I want to appreciate the organisers for putting together such a good race and giving athletes like us the platform to compete and challenge ourselves.”

Raymond, who finished second, said he was pleased with his performance and excited to have secured a place among the leading athletes.

“I’m glad and excited to have been a winner. It feels really good to see all the effort and preparation pay off.”

“I’m grateful for the opportunity to compete here, and I want to appreciate the organisers for putting together a race that gives athletes like us the platform to compete and challenge ourselves,” he said.

Gyang, who completed the men’s podium, said he was delighted to finish among the top three and expressed hope that the initiative would continue to grow.

“I’m just happy to be one of the people to grace the podium. It is a good feeling to finish among the top athletes, especially in a race like this. I appreciate the organisers for giving us the opportunity to compete, and I hope this initiative continues to grow and attract even more athletes in the years ahead,” he said.

In the women’s category, Akanbi said the victory was particularly satisfying after the work that went into her preparation.

She also praised the organisers for creating an opportunity for athletes to compete.

“I am very happy to have won the women’s race. It was not easy, but I am glad that all the hard work paid off. I commend the organisers for creating this opportunity and for the effort they put into making the race a success. I hope the Abeokuta 10km Race continues to grow and gives more athletes the chance to compete at this level,” she said.

The race was organised by Nilayo Sports Management Limited and attracted sports enthusiasts, dignitaries and residents from different parts of Abeokuta.

Managing director Yetunde Olopade said the organisers were pleased with the outcome and praised the athletes and participants for their commitment throughout the event.

She also thanked the Ogun State Government, sponsors and partners, including Phlo, Bet9ja Foundation, 7UP and Aquafina, for supporting the race.

“We are delighted with the outcome of this year’s Abeokuta 10km Race. The quality, organisation and enthusiasm shown by the participants have once again demonstrated what can be achieved when everyone comes together.

“We appreciate the Ogun State Government, our sponsors, partners and everyone who contributed to making this race a colourful and successful event. Nilayo Sports Management Limited will continue to uphold the class and quality that the company is known for,” Mrs Olopade said.

The Director General of the National Sports Commission, Bukola Olopade, also used the event to highlight the wider opportunities being created for athletes as sporting events continue to grow across Nigeria.

He particularly pointed to the equal prize money for the men’s and women’s winners, saying such measures could help promote equality in sport.

“I have always been a fan of equality. When you look at what Nilayo has done here, giving the same prize money to the men and women, it is something we should encourage,” he said.

“The Nigerian sporting ecosystem is getting bigger, and with events like this, we are creating more avenues for our sportsmen and women to thrive, compete and earn a living from sport.”

Also speaking after the race, the Special Adviser to the President on Media and Public Communication, Chief Sunday Dare, praised Nilayo Sports Management Limited for staging another road race and commended Abeokuta residents for their support.

Mr Dare said the event demonstrated the potential for Nigeria to host high-quality sporting competitions while encouraging participation in sports and healthy living.

“Nilayo has once again demonstrated that we can organise world-class sporting events in Nigeria. This is a top-class event, and the turnout of the people of Abeokuta shows the passion Nigerians have for sports and healthy living,” he said.

The race also provided an opportunity for residents to participate in fitness activities while highlighting Abeokuta’s potential as a destination for road racing and other sporting events.

Among the dignitaries present were the Ogun State Commissioner for Sports Development, Wasiu Isiaka; the Special Adviser to the Ogun State Governor on Youth Development, Tunde Delu; former Ogun State Commissioner for Women Affairs, Adijat Motunrayo Adeleye; and former members of the Ogun State House of Assembly, Femi Allen Taylor and Idowu Olowofuja.

World.title: ‘A huge moment for me’: Omogbeja reacts to Ondo 50 Sports Icons Award
World.content:
Veteran sports journalist Yomi Omogbeja has described his recognition at the Ondo 50 Sports Icons Award as a pleasant surprise and a homecoming, reflecting on his family’s historical connection with sports administration in the state.

Mr Omogbeja, editor-in-chief of Athletics Africa, was among 50 sports personalities, administrators, media organisations and institutions honoured by the Sports Writers Association of Nigeria (SWAN), Ondo State Chapter, for their contributions to sports development.

The award ceremony, held in Akure, was part of activities marking the 50th anniversary of Ondo State’s creation.

Reacting to the honour in a statement to Premium Times, Mr Omogbeja said he was particularly moved by the recognition despite living far from home.

“It was a pleasant surprise and a great privilege for me to receive the award. It’s particularly heartwarming for me and felt good to be remembered even when one is so far from home,” he said.

He described the recognition as a homecoming of sorts, recalling that his father served as an executive member of the Ondo State Sports Council in the 1980s.

“It’s like a homecoming of sorts because my Dad used to be an Executive member of the Ondo State Sports Council in the 80s,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Omogbeja said being recognised alongside prominent figures, including former Ondo State Governor Olusegun Mimiko and former Nigeria Professional Football League (NPFL) chairman Gbenga Elegbeleye, made the occasion particularly significant.

“And to be so honoured among eminent personalities like the former Governor of Ondo State, Dr Olusegun Mimiko; former Chairman of the Nigeria Professional Football League (NPFL), Otunba Gbenga Elegbeleye; and many more distinguished sons and daughters of our state is a huge moment for me,” he added.

Three decades of sports journalism

Mr Omogbeja, who hails from Idogun in Ose Local Government Area of Ondo State, has more than 30 years of experience in sports journalism, with a career spanning traditional and digital media.

He is the editor-in-chief of Athletics Africa, which was launched in July 2004 as Africa’s first dedicated track and field news and events platform.

His professional experience includes coverage of major FIFA and Confederation of African Football (CAF) tournaments, as well as multiple International Association of Athletics Federations (IAAF), now World Athletics, indoor, cross-country and outdoor championships and Olympic Games since 1999.

He has also worked with several media organisations, including The News/Tempo, Punch Newspapers, National Interest Newspapers and Africa Oil+Gas Report. He was among the pioneer planning and online editors of the defunct 234NEXT.com when it launched in 2008.

His international experience includes working as a producer and editorial manager for local content at West-Midlands Cable Ananova.com in Leeds, United Kingdom.

Beyond journalism, Mr Omogbeja has collaborated with media organisations, national sports federations and government ministries in Nigeria, Ghana and Zimbabwe on digital transformation, new media solutions and strategic communications.

His academic qualifications include master’s degrees in Web Journalism from the University of Sheffield, Sociology and Psychology of Sports from the University of Ibadan, and Olympic Studies from the German Sport University Cologne. He also holds a professional diploma in Digital Marketing, Sponsorship and Communications from Barça Universitas.

His contributions to sports journalism have earned him several distinctions, including the Telkom/SABC/Highway Africa Innovation Award for Journalism in 2011 and recognition as a finalist in the 2004 Press Gazette UK Student Online Journalist of the Year awards.

In October 2025, he was inducted as a Fellow of SWAN (FSWAN) and received the association’s Veteran Sports Journalist Award during its Diamond Jubilee celebration.

World.title: Soludo swears in council chairmen, demands accountability
World.content:
By Vincent Ujumadu

Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has sworn in the newly elected 21 local government chairmen and their deputies, charging them to prioritise service delivery, accountability and responsible use of public resources.

The governor urged the officials to take their oath of office seriously, review it regularly and consider displaying it in visible locations as a constant reminder of their responsibilities.

“As you begin your journey, know that it is a call to serve,” Soludo told the chairmen, urging them to be their brothers’ and sisters’ keepers, which he said was in line with the agenda of the ruling All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA).

He said the officials should put aside their expectations and immediately focus on the responsibilities of office.

“I know that when you were applying for the job, you had all manner of aspirations, promises and expectations. Welcome to the world of reality and the clock starts ticking today. The work has already begun,” he said.

Soludo also emphasised the need for the officials to account for their time in office, noting that even the minutes spent at the swearing-in ceremony had already become part of their official responsibilities.

The governor noted what he described as APGA’s dominance in Anambra State over the past 20 years, saying the party’s candidates had, in the latest council election, faced little opposition in many areas.

He reminded the chairmen that previous administrations had helped build the structures on which they were assuming office, urging them to leave the local government system stronger for their successors.

Soludo also urged the new council leaders to embrace innovation while ensuring that their actions remained within the law.

He specifically called for measures to make the local government system more sustainable, noting that the new local government laws permitted councils to pool resources for the effective management of common financial obligations.

The governor advised the chairmen to study the handover notes from their predecessors and carefully assess the assets and liabilities they had inherited, given the challenges confronting the councils.

The swearing-in followed the declaration of the results of the local government election conducted on August 30, 2026.

World.title: IGP deploys DIG, CPs to Imo for corps members’ rescue
World.content:
IGP Disu

By Kingsley Omonobi

The Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Rilwan Disu, has deployed the Deputy Inspector-General of Police in charge of Operations, DIG Shehu Umar Nadada, to Imo State to coordinate the rescue of prospective National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members and other passengers abducted along the Owerri-Onitsha Expressway on Thursday, October 1, 2026.

The Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Aniete Etuk, disclosed this in a statement issued on Saturday in Abuja.

According to the statement, Nadada arrived in Imo with two Commissioners of Police and conducted an on-the-spot assessment of the situation and the ongoing search-and-rescue operation.

The statement said the DIG also reviewed the operational strategies, deployment of personnel and operational assets, and issued further directives to strengthen the coordinated response.

The assessment was conducted alongside the Imo State Commissioner of Police, CP Audu Bosso; the Commissioner of Police in charge of Federal Operations, CP Akpan Anifiok; the Commissioner of Police in charge of the Police Mobile Force; other service commanders and members of the management team of the Imo State Police Command.

The police said the search-and-rescue operation had been intensified, with additional tactical teams and operational assets deployed to identified areas, supported by intelligence-led tracking of the abductors.

The statement said the police were also working closely with other security agencies to secure the safe rescue of the abducted persons and apprehend those responsible.

The statement quoted Nadada as assuring the public that the Nigeria Police Force remained committed to rescuing the 20 abducted persons and would sustain the operation until its conclusion.

He urged members of the public and the media to remain calm and vigilant, while calling on anyone with credible information that could assist the operation to contact the police or the nearest security formation.

The statement assured that all information received would be treated with strict confidentiality and that further updates would be provided as the operation progresses.

World.title: Iranian UN delegation duo ‘kicked out’ of US – State Dept
World.content:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio (Photo by Brendan SMIALOWSKI / AFP)

The United States has “kicked out” two members of the Iranian delegation who attended the recent UN General Assembly after they ignored an order to leave the country, the State Department said Saturday.

“Two more members of the Iranian delegation were found still in (New York) long after the United Nations General Assembly had passed. They have now been kicked out of the US,” a US official told AFP, adding that Secretary of State Marco Rubio “means business.”

US media reported the State Department had told Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and his delegation to leave the country Monday, and resorted to expelling the two members after learning from the Iranian mission to the UN they remained in the country on Friday.

One member of the delegation left Friday night, while the second departed Saturday morning, according to Axios.

US and Iranian officials had met the week prior in New York on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly.

US President Donald Trump had rejected a proposal from Tehran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, but told US media he expected talks to resume in the coming days.

Iranian state news agency IRNA reported that Tehran had no more direct talks scheduled with Washington.

AFP

World.title: Benue Boat Mishap: Govt arrests boat driver, suspends maritime workers’ union
World.content:
By Peter Duru, Makurdi

The Benue State government has suspended the Buruku crossing point branch of the Nigeria Union of Maritime Workers, NUMW, following Saturday’s boat mishap, with several passengers still unaccounted for.

The state Commissioner for Marine and Blue Economy, Denis Iyaghigba, ordered the immediate suspension of the union after conducting an on-the-spot assessment of the scene of the accident.

The Commissioner also ordered the suspension of the line operator and directed the arrest and detention of the boat skipper involved in the mishap.

The measures, according to the government, were part of immediate steps to prevent a recurrence of the incident and ensure compliance with safety regulations at the state’s waterways.

The government, in a statement issued by the Head, Media and Public Orientation, Office of the Commissioner for Marine and Blue Economy, Lubem Gena, said the Ministry had activated its search and rescue operations following the accident.

It said the search operation was being conducted in collaboration with local divers to intensify efforts to locate passengers who remained unaccounted for.

According to the statement, “the Benue state government has suspended the Buruku crossing point branch of the Nigeria Union of Maritime Workers, NUMW, following Saturday’s boat mishap in which several passengers remain unaccounted for despite the rescue of others.”

The Commissioner, who visited the scene of the incident, also directed that the line operator be suspended while the boat skipper be arrested and detained pending further investigation into the circumstances surrounding the accident.

The statement quoted Iyaghigba as saying that the government was determined to establish what led to the mishap and take measures to prevent similar incidents on the state’s waterways.

“The Ministry has since activated its search and rescue processes and is working with local divers to intensify the search and rescue,” the Commissioner said.

He disclosed that an inter-ministerial committee had also been constituted to investigate the incident and establish its immediate, remote and underlying causes.

Iyaghigba said the committee would interrogate the circumstances surrounding the mishap and make recommendations aimed at strengthening safety standards at river crossing points across the state.

He further ordered strict compliance with the mandatory use of life jackets at all river crossing points in the state.

According to him, the directive was part of measures to strengthen safety and protect passengers using waterways across Benue.

The Commissioner also raised concern over an abandoned barge at the crossing point which was believed to have contributed to the accident. He consequently gave the owner of the abandoned barge a seven-day ultimatum to evacuate it from the crossing point or risk having it confiscated by the state government.

The statement said the Commissioner would work closely with relevant Ministries, Departments and Agencies, MDAs, during the week to further interrogate the circumstances surrounding the accident and strengthen safety measures across the state’s waterways.

“The government said further details would be made available, but at the moment, investigations and rescue efforts continue,” the statement added.

The latest development followed the boat mishap at the Buruku crossing point on Saturday morning where a wooden boat conveying passengers capsized while crossing the River Katsina-Ala.

Several passengers were rescued following the accident, while others were reported missing, prompting the activation of search and rescue operations by the state government.

World.title: Brain surgery in 2015 affected my penis – Julius Agwu
World.content:
Nigerian comedian and actor Julius Agwu has opened up about a personal complication which followed the brain surgery he had in the United States.

Agwu underwent brain surgery in 2015 after doctors reportedly discovered three tumours in his brain. One of the tumours was said to be about the size of a golf ball.

Agwu disclosed that he experienced a loss of sexual function after the procedure, revealing the previously little-discussed impact during a recent episode of the Beer Parlour Talk Show uploaded on Saturday.

The comedian was discussing the effects of his health battle on his body, career and personal life when the host asked if the brain condition or surgery had affected other aspects of his health, including his sexual function.

Agwu responded, “After I do am, prick no dey work again now. He no dey work.”

Other participants on the programme, including Mr Patrick, subsequently discussed the nerve involved in the surgery and its connection to the brain as they sought to explain the effect Agwu described.

Agwu also reflected on his influence on Nigeria’s comedy industry, particularly his role in popularising the combination of music and comedy.

“Music comedy na me form am o, that is to tell you how my brain dey work,” he said.

The conversation later became emotional as Agwu broke down in tears while reflecting on his career, relationships and the people he felt abandoned him during his difficult period.

“God wey I dey serve, anybody wey get hand for wetin happen to me. I go dey look. My friends deserted me. They stopped talking to me, many of them. It is well,” he said.

World.title: Tinubu saved Nigeria from collapse – Shettima
World.content:
VP Shettima

By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

Vice President Kashim Shettima has defended President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms, saying the nation was “teetering on the verge of collapse” before the withdrawal of fuel subsidy and unification of exchange rates.

The Vice President urged Nigerians to be “generous” to a leader he credits with saving the economy.

Speaking after a meeting with Tinubu at the President’s Lagos residence, Shettima said the administration had been in “regular contact” with the President throughout his sojourn abroad and was “updating him on developments in the nation.”

“We are quite thrilled that he is back on the beat, and we have been in regular contact throughout his sojourn abroad,” Shettima said.

“Advances in science and technology have made it possible to really have impactful leadership wherever one might find himself. So we have been in regular contact. We speak almost every other day, and we are updating him.

“He saved the economy… saved the nation from falling to pieces”

While defending Tinubu’s policies, the Vice President insisted that the decisions to remove the petrol subsidy and realign multiple exchange rates were “far-reaching” and necessary to avert economic disaster.

“As usual, impactful decision-making that will touch the lives of the Nigerian people. It’s absolutely essential that Nigerians need to be generous to this poor man,” Shettima said.

“When we assumed the mantle of leadership, our foreign reserves was a staggeringly low 3.9 billion dollars — that was not enough to import oil for one month. He had the courage and the conviction to take far-reaching decisions.

“The withdrawal of the fuel subsidy, the realignment of the multiple exchange rates, were far-reaching decisions.”

“He literally… the economy was actually teetering on the verge of collapse. He saved the economy. I want Nigerians to understand this fundamental truism.

“We are on the road to Caracas. He saved our economy. He saved the nation from falling to pieces,” Shettima added.

Acknowledging the hardship many Nigerians face, Shettima struck a defiant tone, insisting that relief programmes are already in the pipeline.
