Talking about open, predictable and rule-based global economic relationships, Sitharaman said nations should engage with one another through dialogue and negotiated agreements, rather than allowing geopolitical differences to become barriers to trade and investment.

World.title: Protesters in Hyderabad demand CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation, scrapping of SIR
World.content:
A protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and the scrapping of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls was held at Dharna Chowk in Hyderabad on Saturday (October 3, 2026), with demonstrators alleging that the exercise could exclude large sections of voters from the electoral rolls.

The protest began with a Hindi rendition of Bella Ciao, the Italian anti-resistance song, with protesters dubbing SIR as ‘Special Intensive Resistance’. The demonstration was organised by 12 organisations, including the Telangana unit of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and the Telangana People’s Front (TPF).

The three demands

The protesters raised three demands, the resignation of Mr. Gyanesh Kumar, selection of the Chief Election Commissioner through a process that includes the Chief Justice of India (CJI), and scrapping of the SIR exercise.

Speakers at the protest gathering alleged that the SIR was the National Register of Citizens (NRC) through the back door. The allegations came amid a wider national controversy over the deletion of names from electoral rolls during the revision exercise. The protesters claimed that 13 crore names had been excluded from draft electoral rolls across States and Union Territories.

M.V. Reddy, a TPF member, described the scale of the deletions as unprecedented, saying that while several electoral revisions had been carried out in the past, none had resulted in such a large number of names being removed.

Akunuri Murali, former chairperson of the Telangana Education Commission, read out the Preamble to the Constitution during the protest, with demonstrators raising their right hands and repeating the words after him. Sunita Regunta of the National Alliance of People’s Movements said the organisation had been following the SIR process since it began in Bihar ahead of the State’s elections. She alleged that the exercise was disproportionately affecting people without the resources or means to navigate the process and was removing them from electoral rolls.

Although the protest was scheduled to begin at 10 a.m., people arrived gradually, with the gathering growing to around 100 participants by 11 a.m. at Dharna Chowk.

Sameer of the Students’ Federation of India (SFI) drew a parallel with the protests over the NEET question-paper leak, saying the mobilisation of Gen Z over the issue had demonstrated the impact of sustained public pressure. He called for similar mobilisation against the SIR process.

Usman, general secretary of the Association for Protection of Civil Rights (APCR), said a large section of society continued to remain unconcerned about developments in the country. He alleged that the SIR could exclude people who sought to strengthen democratic institutions and stressed that voting was a fundamental part of democratic participation.

Sreeja of the Disha Students Organisation said SIR was normally intended to increase voter enrolment but was instead being used to delete voters. She also alleged that the ruling party had concluded that Gen Z would not support it following the police lathicharge during protests in Delhi.

Kancha Ilaiah, Dalit rights activist and former Professor of political science at Osmania University, recalled the functioning of the Election Commission during the Emergency. He said the institution had remained independent even then, pointing to the subsequent election of Janata Party as an example of the importance of an independent electoral process.

Cyber security activist Srinivas Kodali raised concerns about linking different databases through the SIR process. He questioned how voter identities could be reliably established when Aadhaar itself had not been properly created for everyone, and alleged that the process could eventually be incorporated into an NRC-like exercise. Mr. Kodali also said the movement against SIR should continue even if Mr. Kumar resigned, pointing to the upcoming Census and the wider implications of linking citizens’ lives and identities to government databases.

World.title: CaRWAN protests ‘unlawful’ arrests of Noida workers, activists near Jantar Mantar, 70 detained
World.content:
Amid the ongoing protests over the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, the Campaign for Release of Workers and Activists of Noida (CaRWAN) on Saturday staged a separate protest near Jantar Mantar seeking the release of workers and activists jailed in connection with the April 13 Noida workers’ protest.

More than 100 protesters marched from Patel Chowk towards Jantar Mantar, and Delhi Police detained at least 70 of them before releasing them later in the day. The protesters alleged that the police forcefully detained and manhandled them, with female protesters allegedly being held by male officers.

‘Unlawful detention’

CaRWAN demanded that workers and activists who had been “unlawfully held by Uttar Pradesh Police and incarcerated for over five months” be released immediately.

“While there are protests going on against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, his daughter Medha Roopam, who is the District Magistrate of Gautam Buddha Nagar, issued NSA detention orders against Satyam Verma and Akriti Chaudhary,” CaRWAN member Anjali said during the protest.

Ms. Anjali said that while Mr. Verma, a translator and former journalist, continues to be detained under the National Security Act (NSA), 1980, Ms. Chaudhary remains in jail despite the Allahabad High Court quashing her detention under the NSA on September 2.

Six others, including activist Aditya Anand, workers Manisha and Rupesh, student leaders Yogesh Meena and Himanshu Thakur and artist Srishti Gupta are also in jail. The police have registered 11 FIRs against them.

“The Allahabad High Court called the police investigation on the basis of which the order was issued a ‘concocted story’ while quashing Ms. Chaudhary’s detention. The Uttar Pradesh government and police have been acting unlawfully since day one and people who have been working for social causes on the ground have been facing the brunt of it,” Ms. Anjali said.

For a cause

The protesters sat down near Jantar Mantar after the police asked them to clear the site. The police then allegedly forcefully took them into three buses, where female protesters were held by male officers and others were pushed and pulled by police personnel. Two buses were taken to Sector 23 Dwarka police station and one to Kapashera, where the detainees were later released, Ms. Anjali said.

“Female protesters were detained after 6 p.m.,” said Chitranshu, a protester.

Naureen, another member of CaRWAN, said the Uttar Pradesh police had tried to fabricate evidence and plant a mobile phone at Ms. Gupta’s house. “The police, working in alignment with the government, do not have any real evidence against them. We demand that they be released immediately,” she said.

Delhi University Professors Nandita Narain and N. Sachin were also part of the protest.

“Journalists like Satyam Verma and activists who are role models for all citizens have been held illegally and put behind bars. Regressive laws like the NSA have been imposed on them. These show the brutalities of both the police and those in power,” Ms. Narain said.

World.title: Nolo becomes Category 3 Hurricane in remote Pacific Ocean
World.content:
Nolo strengthened into a major hurricane on Saturday (October 3, 2026) far out in the Pacific Ocean, well to the west of Hawaii’s main islands.

The storm’s maximum sustained winds rapidly intensified to 115 mph (185 kph), the Miami-based National Hurricane Center reported, meaning it was a Category 3 hurricane.

Nolo was located about 210 miles (335 kilometres) south-southwest of Maro Reef and moving westward at 17 mph (28 kph).

A tropical storm warning was issued for the Papahanaumokuakea Marine National Monument — a massive and remote federally protected area with islands, atolls, seamounts, shoals and coral reefs — from Maro Reef to Lisianski Island.

The hurricane centre said large surf associated with Nolo “will likely inundate some of the low-lying atolls.”

No threat was in the forecast for any populated islands, however.

The hurricane centre said Nolo was expected to cross the international date line on Sunday (October 4, 2026).

Nolo skirted Hawaii as a hurricane a week ago. It then lost some of its punch and became a tropical storm before regaining hurricane strength on Friday (October 2, 2026).

Meanwhile, another Pacific hurricane, Category 1 Rachel, continued heading westward on a path away from the west coast of Mexico.

Dangerous swells were forecast through the weekend for the coast of west-central Mexico and through Monday (October 5, 2026) for the Baja California Peninsula, according to the hurricane centre.

World.title: UGD work on Mettupalayam Road leads to sewage backflow into street manholes in Coimbatore
World.content:
Ongoing underground drainage (UGD) pipeline shifting work on Mettupalayam Road has led to backflow from manholes and waterlogging in parts of neighbouring wards in Coimbatore for over a week.

Residents of Wards 44, 45 and 69 said the problem had affected several streets in K.K. Pudur and surrounding areas, with foul-smelling wastewater entering stormwater drains and accumulating at low-lying points on roads.

V. Swathi of Ramasamy Street in K.K. Pudur, Ward 44, said a manhole had been overflowing throughout the day for more than a week. “The foul smell has become a major problem, and the stagnant wastewater is causing hygiene concerns,” she said.

Baby Sudha, councillor of Ward 45, said problems with the UGD system had been reported in the area since the construction of the flyover. “The present work has aggravated the problem. Four streets in the ward are severely affected by the backflow. We have also requested the officials to complete the work at the earliest,” she said.

A senior Corporation official said the UGD pipeline shifting work began beneath the Saibaba Colony flyover near Anna Market recently. A section of the pipeline located close to the flyover pillars had to be shifted to the service roads.

The work is being carried out by the Highways Department. The shifting of the pipeline had disrupted the normal flow in the network, resulting in complaints from neighbouring areas, the official said. “We have instructed the Highways Department to complete the work within a week,” the official said.

World.title: Legendary movie director, writer Singeetham Srinivasa Rao passes away
World.content:
Legendary cinema director and writer Singeetham Srinivasa Rao passed away on Saturday evening in Chennai in Kauvery Hospital, according to family and friends. He was 94.

Born in Gudur in Nellore district, he burst onto the screen at the age of 41 with his writing and direction of Neeti Nijayati, a Telugu movie with a homily in its heart in 1972. But before that, Singeetham began as a dialogue writer to filmmaker K.V. Reddy and assisted him in the ground breaking Telugu movie in 1957: Mayabazar. Between these two dates, he honed and experimented his craft.

From then onwards, he directed movies in multiple languages including Pushpak Vimana without any dialogue starring Kamal Hassan an Amala. Among the notable movies he helmed or had a role in bringing to screen were: Pantulamma, Zamindaru Gari Ammayi, America Ammayi, Pilla Zamindar, Mayuri, Apoorva Sagodharargal, Michael Madana Kama Rajan, Aditya 369 and dozens of other movies.

Also read | ‘Pushpak’ at 35: A sit down with legendary filmmaker Singeetam Srinivasa Rao

Singeetham Srinivasa Rao acted in some movies and even composed the movie score. His last movie was the Sing Geetham, musical-fantasy comedy which he directed and wrote the script. The genre defying movie was released in June 2026 with the director sometimes remotely wielding the mike.

World.title: The enduring impact of Singeetham Srinivasa Rao’s films on contemporary filmmakers
World.content:
In one of the conversations hosted by Kamal Haasan’s production house, Raaj Kamal Films International, more than a year ago to celebrate the genius of filmmaker Singeetham Srinivasa Rao, when Suhasini Mani Ratnam asked the director “why a silent film?” while discussing Pushpak, the director responded, “why not?” That moment encapsulates the courage with which he and his several collaborators took unprecedented leaps of faith in his nearly 70-year career in cinema. At 94, his new Telugu film Sing Geetham, a musical fantasy in which the story will unfold through songs, rather than conversations, will arrive in theatres on June 12.

Produced by writer-director Nag Ashwin for Vyjayanthi Films, Sing Geetham is powered by Devi Sri Prasad’s music and a young team led by executive director Sankalp Gora. Singeetham, who began his career as an assistant director to KV Reddy for the 1957 magnum opus Maya Bazar, has been a mentor for Nag Ashwin’s Savitri biopic Mahanati, and Kalki 2898AD. Several Telugu and Tamil filmmakers have, over the years, mentioned how the veteran director has been a guiding force and an inspiration, encouraging them to explore diverse genres.

The idea of a story narrated in a musical format, Singeetham stated in the pre-release event in Hyderabad, emerged more than 40 years ago. Ahead of his new film, we asked three filmmakers how some of Singeetham’s iconic films had inspired or influenced their work.

‘He did not mimic a success formula’

Vivek Athreya, writer-director

In my formative years, I loved watching Vichitra Sodarulu (Apoorva Sagodharargal), Pushpaka Vimanam (Pushpak), Aditya 369 and Bhairava Dweepam. When I learnt that all these films were from the same director, I was surprised at his exploration of genres. I would term Singeetham garu an Indian Steven Spielberg for my generation. Spielberg’s ET brought out the child in every adult watching the film. It’s similar in the case of Singeetham’s films.

As a filmmaker, I know how tough it is to not mimic a success formula. Singeetham is a versatile filmmaker and a gifted storyteller. When the actor Nani, who knew the premise of Sing Geetham, narrated it to me, I was surprised at the freshness of the idea.

None of his films are easy in terms of craft. Each time I watch Appu as the dwarf in Vichitra Sodarulu or the mirror scene in Michael Madana Kama Rajan where we see the reflection of two of Kamal Haasan’s characters, I wonder how they managed to do it.

In Telugu, Balakrishna’s acting in Singeetham’s films is so different from his work in other films. He brings out the best in his actors. Singeetham’s films also have good music. Brundavanam was a childhood favourite.

The child in Singeetham is still alive, which is why he pulls off the impossible. His statement that “routine cinema is risky, but risky cinema is a safe bet” underlines his confidence that the audience will appreciate a film when offered something new. One of his biggest strengths lies in his collaboration with Kamal Haasan, writers Panchu Arunachalam, Crazy Mohan and others who were equally determined to push the envelope. The writing gave so much depth to Appu’s story, which can move me to tears even today.

‘The wit and humour in his films felt genuine’

Mohana Krishna Indraganti, writer-director

If a filmmaker wants to be versatile, the trap of predictability has to be broken early in their career so that the audience and the trade do not expect similar films. Singeetham garu managed to do that early, rather than jolting his audience after they got acclimatised to a pattern. It takes courage to explore different genres with each film. What makes his journey special is that he did it when most filmmakers stuck to mainstream tropes and formulas. I have had the chance to spend time with him a few times and came away with admiration for his passion for cinema.

What he has managed to do through films such as Michael Madana Kama Rajan (MMKR), Pushpaka Vimanam, Amavasya Chandrudu (Raaja Paarvai) and Apoorva Sagodharargal is no mean feat; these are among my favourite films. Very few filmmakers have managed to direct such diverse films in India.

Some of my comedies have been subtly influenced by the genuine wit and humour in his films. I must have watched MMKR eight or nine times. The word play that we see in the dialogues is a mark of sharp writing. He was also fortunate to collaborate with writers and actors like Crazy Mohan and Kamal Haasan. I am not sure if such collaborations are even possible today.

‘The drama stands out in Singeetham’s films’

Venkatesh Maha, writer-director

I have often stated that the inspiration for my films come from my experiences and observations. However, of late, I have realised how certain filmmakers have subconsciously influenced my work. There is a lot of drama in Singeetham garu’s films, be it in comic or emotional sequences, that emerges from the writing. Take the character of a beggar portrayed by PL Narayana in Pushpak. We see visuals of him with a lot of money and yet, when he dies a lonely life, it makes the protagonist think about the futility of wealth in the absence of people.

Michael Madana Kama Rajanis a classic in how it explores comedy and within it, contains a lot of drama. I am also reminded of a scene in Brundavanam where Rajendra Prasad and Ramya Krishnan go incognito into the city.

As a child, I was fascinated by how Aditya 369 showed time travel and Bhairava Dweepam explored a fantasy drama. I also remember trying to mimic Kamal Haasan’s Appu act. Unlike today when filmmakers are in a rush to move to the next shot, the camera unapologetically stays on Appu when he is heartbroken, long enough to make us empathise with him and weep along.

Singeetham garu never hesitates to try something new. A filmmaker must be fearless and enthusiastic from deep within to do that. I was introduced to the film Mayuri by my mother and I was shocked to learn that it was Sudha Chandran’s true story.

Beyond the larger exploration of new ideas and experiments with crafts and techniques, the focus on finer details made his films entertaining. For instance, listen to the chorus in the song ‘Madhurame Sudhaganam’ in Brundavanam. In some portions, the singers’ voice modulation recreates how the sound moved from left to the right in stereos of the 80s and 90s. It is things like these that make his films memorable.

World.title: Tennessee’s prisons chief is resigning after failed execution of Christa Pike
World.content:
The head of Tennessee's prison system is resigning, Governor Bill Lee announced Saturday (October 3, 2026), the first major staff shake-up since Christa Pike's stunning failed execution left her unconscious and on a ventilator at a hospital.

Frank Strada, commissioner of the Department of Correction, will step down this month, Mr. Lee said. Some of the Governor's fellow Republicans and other elected officials had been urging a change in leadership.

It was the second time since May that Tennessee had not been able to execute a prisoner who was seemingly moments away from death.

The Governor also announced that former U.S. Attorney Ed Stanton would lead a review of what happened in Pike's death chamber. Stanton was previously named to conduct a review after Lee called off a different execution in 2022; he found in that case that Tennessee had not complied with its own lethal injection process.

Mr. Strada said in a statement that resigning was “in the best interest of Tennesseans” while Stanton's review is conducted. The state failed to execute Pike despite administering two doses of a lethal drug, pentobarbital.

Pike, now 50, was 18 when she and her boyfriend tortured and killed a classmate, Colleen Slemmer, in a jealous rage in 1995. She became one of the youngest women to be sent to death row.

There was no immediate response from Pike's lawyers for an update on Saturday (October 3, 2026) on her condition at a hospital. They had disclosed on Friday (October 2, 2026) that she was on a ventilator and unconscious in the hours following the execution attempt and that hospital staff were trying to clear the two doses of pentobarbital.

The shocking failure has left both sides of the death penalty debate demanding answers. Mr. Lee has ordered an independent review and halted any new executions. Mr. Strada said he believes the state “carried out its responsibilities in accordance with the established protocol.”

Pike's legal team welcomed Mr. Strada's departure but said “it does nothing to help Christa now.”

“What happened to her Wednesday reflects a systemic failure that goes far beyond any one person,” the four-lawyer team said. “We hope the governor’s call for a full, independent review will expose the profound problems within Tennessee’s entire death penalty system.”

Pike’s attorneys said they believed problems with the IV lines caused the pentobarbital to flow into her body instead of her bloodstream.

Pike was extraordinarily cooperative with the execution team, even instructing them to “please try here, please try here” as they tried to insert lines, lawyer Randy Spivey told reporters Thursday (October 1, 2026).

In May, Tennessee stopped the execution of Tony Carruthers after staff placed an IV into his right arm but couldn’t get a secondary IV line. The Governor ordered officials to wait at least a year before trying to execute him again.

Mr. Strada took over the Correction Department in January 2023 after serving as deputy director of the Arizona Department of Corrections. In late 2024, he announced that Tennessee was changing its lethal injection protocol and would use only pentobarbital.

Four people have been executed in Tennessee since 2025, according to the Correction Department.

Court filings show that Mr. Strada's job included overseeing executions in Arizona when they resumed in 2022 following an eight-year break.

Clarence Dixon was the first that year. The medical team had trouble finding a vein to administer the lethal drugs and finally made an incision in his groin area. The process took about 25 minutes.

That same year in Arizona, medical staff preparing Frank Atwood for execution initially could not locate a vein in his right arm but inserted the IV in his right hand — at Mr. Atwood’s suggestion, said Henry Brean, an Arizona Daily Star reporter who was a witness.

Mr. Strada announced Murray Hooper's execution by lethal injection, the third in 2022. There was an unsuccessful attempt to insert an IV line in his right arm. The IV in Hooper's leg was inserted into his femoral artery.

“When Governor Lee hired Strada to fix execution problems in Tennessee, his problematic history of executions in Arizona was well known,” said Kit Thomas, an attorney who has represented people on Tennessee's death row.

World.title: Morning Digest: Protests against CEC persist as Rahul calls for joint ‘resistance’; Indian, Pakistani diplomats summoned over BSF killing two ‘infiltrators’, and more
World.content:
As protests against CEC continue, Rahul launches ‘Satyagraha’ digital platform

As Opposition leaders, civil society activists and youth organisations continued their protests, seeking the removal of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi launched the ‘Satyagraha’ digital platform to map resistance movements across the country. For the second day, the Delhi Police detained around 150 protesters, including All India Students’ Association national president Neha Bora, civil society activists Yogendra Yadav and Anjali Bharadwaj, and Supreme Court advocate Prashant Bhushan, as they marched from Patel Chowk towards Jantar Mantar to demand the removal of the CEC.

Indian and Pakistani diplomats summoned over BSF killing two ‘infiltrators’

India and Pakistan summoned each other’s diplomats and traded charges over the killing of two Pakistani men who the Border Security Force said had attempted to infiltrate through the International Border along Punjab’s Tarn Taran district. Pakistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA) summoned the Indian Charge d’Affaires (CdA) in Islamabad on Saturday (October 3, 2026) to protest the killings of men they said were “unarmed civilians”. Late in the evening, India also summoned the Pakistan Charge d’Affaires to reject the Pakistani statement and protested “the continued facilitation of illegal cross-border infiltration from Pakistan”.

Sheikh Hasina’s extradition possible via ‘well-structured’ process: India’s High Commissioner to Bangladesh

Extradition of Bangladesh’s deposed Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina could take place via a “well-structured process” that involved “legality”, and that a legal process was “in place”, India’s High Commissioner to Bangladesh Dinesh Trivedi said. Speaking of Ms. Hasina’s presence in India at the Bay of Bengal Conversation, an annual conclave organised by the Dhaka-based Centre for Governance Studies, Mr. Trivedi indicated that Ms. Hasina had sought refuge in India based on consultation among those governing Bangladesh in July-August 2024, and that, “India had hardly any choice.”

Hardened narco-trafficking kingpin Navpreet Singh deported from Türkiye: Amit Shah

Union Home Minister Amit Shah said that hardened narco-trafficking kingpin Navpreet Singh has been deported from Türkiye. Mr. Shah said that Mr. Singh was deported to India on Saturday in connection with cases involving drug trafficking and other crimes.

MRFA deal likely by end of FY27, says IAF chief; annual requirement of 36-40 fighters

India expects to finalise the much-awaited Multi-Role Fighter Aircraft (MRFA) deal by the end of the current financial year, provided the ongoing process progresses as planned, Air Chief Marshal A.P. Singh said. The proposed acquisition of 114 fighter aircraft is at the price negotiation stage, with discussions also underway on other critical aspects of the programme. Once concluded, the deal would be the Indian Air Force’s largest fighter aircraft acquisition.

‘I’m a team player, will work as full-back’: New Punjab Congress chief Pargat Singh

Downplaying factionalism in the Punjab Congress, newly appointed State chief Pargat Singh said the team was a good one and all decisions would be taken unanimously, keeping the interests of the State in mind. Mr. Singh, a former hockey player and India captain, said he had always played as a "full-back," a position centred on supporting the team from behind, and would continue to play the same role in the party by giving prominence to other senior members.

Opposition will step up agitation and demand fresh elections using ballot paper: Kharge

Congress president and Leader of the Opposition in the Rajya Sabha, Mallikarjun Kharge, said that the Opposition will step up agitation against the Election Commission of India and demand fresh elections using ballot papers in States where elections were held post SIR process. Mr. Kharge described the Narendra Modi-led Union government as an “illegal government” and demanded that it go, alleging that the democratic and constitutional rights of people were being undermined.

CJP stresses non-violence and urges citizens to join October 10 Delhi protest

The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) stressed that its proposed October 10 protest in Delhi would be peaceful and urged every citizen seeking free and fair elections to join the agitation if Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar does not resign. The CJP has been demanding Mr. Kumar’s resignation, citing alleged irregularities in the electoral processes and the conduct of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise.

Mumbai police question IIT Bombay professor Doolla for 10 hours over student Sahil Wakode’s death

The Mumbai police questioned Suryanarayana Doolla, a professor at the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay (IIT-B), for nearly 10 hours in connection with the death of 22-year-old student Sahil Wakode, an official said. Professor Doolla, who faces allegations of harassment and caste-based discrimination from Mr. Wakode's parents, denied all charges during questioning on Thursday (October 1, 2026), the official said, adding that his statement had been officially recorded.

Delhi Police registers three FIRs over anti-CEC protests, none named

Delhi Police registered at least three FIRs in connection with Friday (October 2) protests by student organisations, political parties and civil society activists who attempted to gather at Jantar Mantar, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Two FIRs were registered at Parliament Street police station and one at Connaught Place police station, invoking Section 223 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) for alleged disobedience of an order duly promulgated by a public servant, a senior police officer said.

TVK to file complaint with ECI against M.K. Stalin’s remarks against its candidate in Dharapuram: Minister

The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) will file a complaint with the Election Commission of India (ECI) against the alleged body-shaming remarks made by Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) president M.K. Stalin about the TVK’s Dharapuram candidate, during his campaign, said Minister C.T.R. Nirmal Kumar. Accusing Mr. Stalin of making derogatory remarks against the TVK candidate, P. Sathyabama, Mr. Nirmal Kumar told reporters in Coimbatore that it was condemnable that Mr. Stalin could say this about a Scheduled Caste woman who was fighting the polls in Dharapuram.

Mumbai airport, airlines clash over Navi Mumbai shift

A dispute is brewing between Adani-run Mumbai International Airport Ltd. (MIAL) and airlines over a proposed operational reshuffle during the phased redevelopment of Terminal 1 (T1). The plan involves moving domestic traffic from T1 to Terminal 2 (T2), while shifting some international services to the more distant Navi Mumbai International Airport.

Delhi Police personnel were removing identity badges before detaining protesters: CPI MP to Amit Shah

CPI MP P. Sandosh Kumar alleged that Delhi Police personnel have been removing or concealing their identity badges before detaining or using force against protesters and urged Union Home Minister Amit Shah to order a time-bound inquiry into the practice. In a letter to the Union Home Minister, Mr. Kumar sought his intervention into repeated use of violence, arbitrary detentions, manhandling and other unlawful practices by the Delhi Police while dealing with democratic protests.

NHRC seeks probe into alleged use of minors at CJP’s Mumbai protest

The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) took cognisance of allegations that minors were involved in a Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led protest in Mumbai and that their images were circulated online. Based on complaints from Sewa Nyaya Utthan Foundation and another organisation, the commission directed the Mumbai Police to investigate the matter and submit an Action Taken Report (ATR) within one week.

Bank robbery videos, Army insiders and arms dealers: Bolarum theft probe reveals wider plot

Weeks before stealing firearms from the Army premises at Bolarum in Secunderabad Cantonment, former Havaldar Upputholla Mallesh allegedly shared bank robbery videos with his cousin and an associate, asking them to study how such heists were carried out. Investigators now say he had built a network comprising serving Army personnel, prospective robbers and alleged arms dealers before the theft on August 30, 2026.

Suvendu claims Mamata faked her leg injury in 2021, promises probe

West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari alleged that former Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee faked her leg injury while campaigning in Nandigram in 2021. Citing medical reports from a government facility, Mr. Adhikari claimed that it showed she did not have any signs of a fracture. “Mamata Banerjee faked her leg injury while campaigning in Nandigram in 2021. This is the report of the Department of Radio Diagnosis of Bangur Institute of Neurosciences, dated March 11, 2021. There is no evidence of a fracture,” Mr. Adhikari said while addressing the press at the State Secretariat.

CBI files charge sheet against RCom, others in ₹3,750 crore LIC fraud case

The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has filed a charge sheet against Reliance Communications Limited (RCom), two former executives of the Reliance (Anil Ambani) Group, and others in the LIC investment fraud case that caused an alleged loss of ₹3,750 crore. The agency identified the former executives as Amitabh Jhunjhunwala, the group managing director, and Vishwas Joshi, senior vice-president of Reliance Capital Limited. P. Venugopal, the then chief investment officer of LIC, has also been named.

SIR exercise: Nine lakh names dropped from Uttarakhand’s poll roll; State now has 71.59 lakh voters

Around nine lakh names have been removed from Uttarakhand’s electoral roll through the special intensive revision (SIR). The final electoral roll was published on Saturday (October 3, 2026) carrying 71.59 lakh electors in the State. Speaking to the media, Uttarakhand Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) B.V.R.C. Purushottam said the final roll includes 1,29,872 newly enrolled voters.

Commander of U.S. Pacific Command to visit India from October 3

Commander of the U.S. Pacific Command Admiral Samuel J. Paparo will visit India from Saturday (October 3, 2026) to Thursday (October 8, 2026) to advance the U.S.-India major defence partnership and deepen military-to-military cooperation between the two countries. According to the U.S. Embassy in India, during his visit, Admiral Paparo is scheduled to engage with his Indian counterparts on a range of shared security priorities, including digital transformation and emerging technologies, regional strategic stability, defence, energy resilience and the challenges posed by an increasingly competitive technology landscape.

Brazil tame India in 4-0 friendly win

Samuel Lino scored his first two goals for ​Brazil as India’s frantic effort to hold off ‌the five-time world champions faded after a ​spirited start, allowing the visitors to ⁠cruise to a 4-0 win in a friendly. Chelsea winger Estevao scored Brazil’s first goal and ‌assisted Pedro before Lino netted a second-half brace, helping Carlo Ancelotti’s side ‌conclude their tour of Australia and India ‌with ⁠two wins and a draw.

World.title: After hours of negotiations, second round of govt-opposition talks ends in a 'deadlock'
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Hours-long negotiations between the government and the opposition during a second round of talks ended in a “deadlock” early on Sunday.

The meeting at Parliament House began after 4pm on Saturday, with discussions focusing on the PTI’s planned Oct 4 march to Islamabad. Details on the negotiating process were sparse as both sides seemingly agreed not to speak to the media before matters concluded.

However, shortly before 3am on Sunday, Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, who was part of the opposition delegation, told the media that the talks had not succeeded in a breakthrough.

“Deadlock,” he told reporters waiting at Parliament House in footage aired on Geo News. Asked what the points of contention were, he said they were “small things”. He added that the “issue” of meetings with PTI founder Imran Khan could not be solved.

He went on to say that the deadlock was over Imran’s meeting with his personal physicians, and how to address terrorism in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. He said that talks had now ended, adding that a detailed press conference would be held later.

Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry, who was part of the government’s delegation in the talks, said the talks failed primarily because the “KP government could not assure whether they would cooperate in the fight against terrorism in the future”.

He alleged that the PTI’s provincial government in KP did not want to implement the National Action Plan and that the PTI delegation that participated in the talks had also left the venue “disappointed because the KP government did not cooperate on terrorism”.

An agreement had been reached on all other matters, he said in response to a question.

Asked about the possible future course of action, he said the “Constitution has several options”, seemingly a referring to the possibility of imposing governor’s rule or emergency in KP.

Separately, PPP’s Sherry Rehman, who also participated in the talks, said the government delegation debated all points with the opposition.

“Unfortunately, the draft [agreement] was changed four times after it was agreed upon,” she told Geo News, adding that she would not go into the details.

Speaking to reporters, PTI interim chairman Barrister Gohar Khan said that the party’s long march was “intact” and would go ahead. At the same time, he asserted that imposing an emergency or governor rule was not the answer to the protest.

He further said that the participants had also not reached an agreement on when the next round of talks would take place.

He said that the opposition’s demands presented during the second round of talks were “simple” and included meetings with Imran and his spouse, Bushra Bibi.

He said that there were a few issues pertaining to terrorism, where the negotiating process became “stuck”.

Hours-long talks

Visuals broadcast by DawnNewsTV after 9:30pm showed Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi — part of the government delegation — departing Parliament House with a document in his hand, with media reports suggesting he was likely to consult the president.

More than an hour later, footage showed Naqvi returning to Parliament House, with the interior minister maintaining his silence as reporters swarmed him for queries.

The meeting, chaired by National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq, was aimed at defusing the country’s ongoing political crisis. The PTI’s planned Oct 4 protest march, aimed at demanding Imran’s release, has emerged as the latest point of contention between the party and the federal government.

Even as extended talks kept hopes for an agreement alive, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi remained adamant on proceeding with PTI’s march to Islamabad.

After voicing his determination on Saturday afternoon — which irked government representatives — the KP CM again took to X at 12:46am to detail the itinerary for the protest march.

Laying out the journey plan, Afridi said PTI supporters from the districts of Tank, Dera Ismail Khan, South Waziristan, North Waziristan, Bannu, and Lakki Marwat will join the long march from Lakki Marwat’s Gandi Chowk Lakki Marwat at 1pm on Oct 4.

The caravan will halt for the night near Karak, from where people will depart at 12:30pm the next day and stay overnight near Kohat.

Then, at 12pm on Oct 6, protesters from Kohat, Hangu, Kurram, and Orakzai will join the convoy, which will move towards Peshawar and spend the night near Mattani.

The KP CM’s post went on to say that the caravan will depart from Budh Bair in Peshawar on Oct 7 afternoon. “The remaining constituencies of Peshawar will join us at Kohat Road Bridge and the Motorway Toll Plaza. And we will spend the night near Charsadda Interchange.”

They would then depart the Charsadda Interchange at 12:30pm on Oct 8 after people from Charsadda and Mohmand join them.

Refraining from detailing the final leg of the trip to the federal capital, Afridi said the people “of entire KP” would gather at Khairabad on Oct 8 and spend the night there. “God willing, the plan for the next phase will be announced there.”

NA speaker hopes for ‘cordial’ talks

When the huddle began, the NA speaker expressed his hope that the talks would proceed in the same “cordial atmosphere” as Friday’s, according to a post on the NA’s X account.

The government side included Naqvi, Tallal Minister for States and Frontier Regions Amir Muqam, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry and Prime Minister’s Adviser on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah.

Rehman, along with MNAs Syed Naveed Qamar and Aijaz Hussain Jakhrani, represented the PPP.

The opposition delegation comprised the Senate opposition leader, PTI interim chairman Gohar Ali Khan, Opposition Chief Whip Amir Dogar, MNA Asad Qaiser, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja and PTI Sindh President Haleem Adil Sheikh.

Prior to the meeting with the government, the opposition held a meeting in which standard operating procedures (SOPs) for the talks were finalised.

It was decided that it would be proposed during the meeting that no one from either side would speak to the media during the talks and that a joint statement would be issued afterwards to avoid any misunderstanding.

Speaking to Dawn, TTAP spokesperson Akhunzada Hussain Ahmed Yousufzai said comments made by PPP’s Rehman on Friday had triggered a controversy, leaving the situation unpleasant until late at night.

“The opposition alliance held a meeting before the start of the talks, during which the government side’s views regarding the law and order situation in KP were discussed. After consultation with the KP chief minister, a response was prepared, which will be presented to the government side during the meeting today,” he said.

For the first time in almost three years, representatives of the federal government and the opposition PTI formally came together on Friday for talks aimed at easing the political tension in the country, and apprised each other of their positions.

Though neither side had shared its specific demands with the media, both were hopeful of a positive outcome from the meeting.

Sources on both sides told Dawn that the PTI wants Imran to be shifted from jail to a hospital for medical treatment, while the government has insisted that the opposition call off its protest march on Islamabad.

In August, PTI announced a long march to Islamabad on Sept 27 against what it called the “illegal imprisonment” of its party founder. However, a couple of days before its scheduled long march, the party postponed the march until Oct 4.

Tariq Fazal objects to KP CM’s remarks

CM Afridi’s Saturday statement vowed to hold the long march on Oct 4 and to prevent a repeat of the events of May 9, 2023.

He said PTI was the largest and most popular political party in Pakistan. “Pakistan is a democratic country whose Constitution grants us the right to peaceful protest.”

Detailing his long march plan, Afridi said an “ocean of people” would begin its journey from Gandi Chowk in Lakki Marwat at 1pm on Oct 4.

The party would continue its struggle until the supremacy of the Constitution and the law was ensured in Pakistan and an independent judiciary was restored, the PTI leader added.

“All demands of the PTI are in accordance with the constitution and the law.”

He stressed that the party would “neither allow May 9 to happen again nor allow anyone else to repeat it”.

Reacting to the KP CM’s remarks, Chaudhry said Afridi’s statements could affect the ongoing negotiation process even though the government wanted them to be “meaningful and fruitful”.

He urged PTI leaders to refrain from making such statements until the final stage of the negotiations, so that the dialogue process was not “harmed”.

“The language that Sohail Afridi is using against his opponents and our leadership does not seem like that of a chief minister; his statements are extremely indecent and reprehensible,” Chaudhry said.

Speaking to reporters ahead of the meeting, PPP’s Rehman stressed that her party was making efforts to solve issues in a democratic manner.

Asked about KP CM being adamant on the PTI march, the PPP leader said it was up to the PTI, but added that she would refrain from making comments before the talks conclude.

While acknowledging that each party had its positions, she noted that the objective of holding negotiations was to “discuss those positions”.

‘Political solutions to political problems’

Separately, PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, an ally of the PML-N government, reiterated his call for PTI to call off its long march.

Speaking at an event in Karachi on Saturday, Bilawal said it was his party that urged the Centre to engage in dialogue with PTI whereas the federal government had “made up its mind” on imposing emergency or governor’s rule in KP.

In a post on X on Friday, the PPP chairman had pressed PTI to unconditionally call off the long march, which he said would allow the country to come together to address the threat of terrorism and threats emanating from neighbouring countries.

Bilawal also welcomed the government’s decision to work with his party and jointly engage with the opposition “to find political solutions to political problems”.

Also on Friday, the army’s top brass warned that any attempt at creating agitation or a “May 9-like situation” would be dealt with “decisive force”.

Ahead of the talks, federal ministers had warned that the Centre would have no option but to impose governor’s rule or an emergency in KP, citing the province’s security situation and the protest call, while PTI had warned of dire consequences if such a step was taken.

The decision to hold talks was taken on Thursday at a presidency meeting attended by President Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Naqvi, Attorney General for Pakistan Mansoor Awan and other PPP and PML-N leaders.

A source privy to the huddle told Dawn the emergency option was discussed, but participants agreed to first give the opposition a chance to settle matters peacefully through dialogue, and to seriously consider an emergency only if the PTI did not back down. The coalition also believes the march will remain confined to KP and not enter Punjab or Islamabad.

On Thursday, Sanaullah said the government and PTI were engaged in “off-the-record talks” over the protest, and that the decision on the march rested with the PTI’s senior leadership, “with whom off-the-record consultation is ongoing”. “So let us see, even if they do not postpone it, we have arrangements in place to stop them,” he warned.

Separately, PM Shehbaz has invited NA Opposition Leader Mehmood Khan Achakzai for dialogue, and the two are expected to meet in the coming days.

World.title: Sanaa, Riyadh rattled by strikes as war widens
World.content:
• Houthis say Saudi aircraft carried out 26 strikes on Yemen capital, claim attack on Aramco facility in south of Riyadh

• Trump’s top national security aides meet secretly on Yemen, Iran

SANAA: Fighting between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthis showed no signs of abating on Saturday, with the Houthis saying the kingdom had launched dozens of strikes on capital Sanaa, while flames and smoke were seen rising from a facility belonging to Saudi oil giant Aramco, south of Riyadh.

While Houthis later said they attacked an Aramco facility with ballistic missiles and drones, there was no immediate confirmation from Saudi Arabia. The foes have traded strikes since the Houthis seized all of Yemen’s Red Sea coast and took control of the Bab al-Mandab strait in a lightning offensive.

US media outlet Axios reported earlier on Friday that US President Donald Trump’s top cabinet members “met secretly at the presidential retreat at Camp David to discuss the Saudi-Houthi conflict in Yemen and next steps in the Iran war”. Vice President Vance chaired the meeting, the news outlet reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

Houthi-affiliated Al-Masirah TV reported that Saudi aircraft hit Sanaa with 26 strikes, after earlier reporting “Saudi aggression” against the Yemeni capital, without providing details on the targets or casualties.

Two AFP correspondents in Sanaa reported hearing loud explosions and seeing warplanes firing missiles on the city.

In neighbouring Saudi Arabia, flames and smoke were seen rising on Saturday afternoon from a facility belonging to state-owned oil giant Aramco south of Riyadh, an AFP journalist said, although both the Houthis and Saudi authorities had yet to comment.

The circumstances remained unclear, though the Houthis have claimed several attacks on facilities belonging to Aramco, majority-owned by the Saudi state, in recent months.

The journalist reported seeing firefighters attempting to extinguish a blaze at the energy giant’s Riyadh refinery, located south of the capital, while ambulances and police vehicles were stationed near the facility.

Al-Masirah TV earlier on Saturday also reported missile strikes on the telecommunications network in Yemen’s northwestern governorate of Saada, one of the group’s strongholds.

It comes after the Houthis said that Saudi Arabia bombed the Yemeni capital itself on Thursday night for the first time since renewed fighting broke out between the two sides in July.

The health ministry in Sanaa claims 72 people have been killed and 125 wounded in Saudi attacks on Yemen since the escalation began, Al Jazeera reports citing the Al Masirah news outlet.

Hunger warning

After several years of calm, Yemen was plunged back into civil war that month, pitting the Houthis, who control most of northwest Yemen including Sanaa, against Yemen’s internationally recognised government.

The government, based in the city of Aden, controls much of the country’s south and east — a region that is larger but much less populated.

Hostilities were reignited after four years of a fragile truce when Iran sent a plane to Sanaa carrying a Houthi delegation.

The flight did not seek authorisation from Saudi Arabia, contravening a practice in place for a decade.

Riyadh retaliated with strikes on Sanaa airport, and in response the Houthis attacked Saudi territory for the first time since 2022.

Since then, fighting has intensified with the Houthis launching a lightning offensive in which they seized control of coastal regions along the Bab al-Mandab strait.

They have also struck multiple Saudi targets including oil infrastructure and the capital Riyadh while also announcing a naval blockade on Saudi shipping in the Red Sea.

Appalling conditions

The renewed fighting has worsened the already appalling humanitarian conditions in Yemen, one of the world’s poorest countries, with the World Food Programme warning on Friday that three-quarters of the population was unable to meet its basic food needs.

Fighting in recent days has centred on Taiz, where dozens of combatants were reported killed on Friday by sources on both sides.

The Houthis reported 55 of their fighters had been killed while government sources told AFP that 26 troops had died.

The battle for Taiz is taking place on several fronts, including highlands overlooking coastal areas recently seized by the Houthis.

While the Houthis have conquered swathes of territory, they have yet to wrest control of Taiz city, which is Yemen’s third-largest after Sanaa and Aden.

The Houthis also on Friday said Saudi Arabia had launched 94 strikes against areas under their control in the past 24 hours.

Saudi authorities meanwhile reported a Houthi projectile had damaged a school in the city of Najran near the Yemen border.

Published in Dawn, October 4th, 2026

World.title: FAO flags gaps in Pakistan’s nutritious food supply
World.content:
• UN agency says over 60pc of citizens unable to afford healthy diet

• Calls for overhaul of agrifood system

ISLAMABAD: The Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) of the United Nations has emphasised the urgent need to transform Pakistan’s agrifood system to improve access to healthy diets, a critical step towards addressing all forms of malnutrition and their related costs to society.

The UN agency, in its latest assessment on “Food Supply for Healthy Diets in Pakistan”, observed that a major challenge in the country’s current food supply is the persistent mismatch between the quantities of food available and those required for the population to consume a healthy diet aligned with the national food-based dietary guidelines (FBDGs).

“Enabling access to healthy diets for all is essential to achieving Pakistan’s national development priorities. Yet over 60 per cent of Pakistanis cannot afford a healthy diet, contributing to the high rates of malnutrition across the country. At the same time, diet-related non-communicable diseases (NCD) are rising, while various forms of undernutrition persist. Unhealthy diets are a common cause of all forms of malnutrition and contribute directly to morbidity and mortality from NCD,” the assessment shows.

The FAO listed priority policy actions to strengthen demand for healthy diets through consumer-focused policies; updating Pakistan’s FBDGs to reflect nutrition, health, and environmental priorities and use it for nutrition education and behavior change; introducing evidence-based fiscal measures, including taxes on sugar-sweetened beverages and other foods high in sugar, salt, and unhealthy fats; introducing front-of-pack nutrition labelling to help consumers make informed food choices; protecting vulnerable populations; restricting the marketing of unhealthy foods, particularly those targeting children, expanding nutritious school meal programmes; and strengthening social protection programmes to improve access to nutritious foods.

The assessment recommended reorienting the agrifood system to deliver healthy diets, aligning agricultural policies and investment priorities to increase support for the production of vegetables, fruits, pulses, roots and tubers across the country, while supporting milk production in some regions; and providing greater incentives for food processors to meet food safety and quality standards and reformulate foods to reduce salt, sugar and unhealthy fats.

It called for promoting healthier retail food environments, through investments in storage, cold chains, and market infrastructure to reduce losses. These actions, combined with regular monitoring, can contri­bute to increasing access to and consumption of healthy diets in Paki­stan, both today and in the future.

The FAO assessment says large gaps were observed for several nutritious food groups, particularly vegetables, roots and tubers, fruits, and legumes and pulses.

However, important misalignment exists between Pakistan’s dietary guidelines and food supply, with supply gaps for several nutritious food groups, particularly vegetables, roots and tubers, fruits, legumes and pulses, while the supply for staples and sugar exceeds what is needed for healthy diets.

“Enabling equitable access to diverse, nutritious, safe, and affordable foods that support healthy diets is a policy imperative for Pakistan,” the assessment said.

Published in Dawn, October 4th, 2026

World.title: Onus on state to protect kids from online harm, IHC told
World.content:
• NCRC recommends boosting NCCIA capacity, setting up special units for exploitation probes • Proposes Peca review from child rights perspective

• Urges integrating age verification into Digital Nation Pakistan Act

ISLAMABAD: Protecting minors from online grooming, exploitation and harmful content is the state’s responsibility, the National Commission on the Rights of Child (NCRC) told the Islamabad High Court while proposing sweeping legal and institutional reforms to safeguard children on social media.

In a 17-page response submitted to the court in a case concerning social media usage by children under the age of 16, the commission acknowledged the concerns raised in the petition.

It underscored the need for age verification mechanisms and a comprehensive regulatory framework, stating that effective legal and regulatory measures are indispensable for online child safety.

The NCRC recommended integrating child online safety into the regulatory framework of the Digital Nation Pakistan Act, with a focus on age verification and effective protection systems.

To combat technology-facilitated child exploitation, the commission recommended boosting the capacity of the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency and establishing specialised systems to investigate online child sexual exploitation.

The commission also recommended a review and amendment of the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca) in the context of child rights, noting the need to improve the existing legal framework for online child safety.

Digital platforms must be made more accountable for child safety, the commission said. It urged effective action against child sexual abuse material and online grooming, while implementing measures for the immediate removal of such content.

“There is also a need to limit unnecessary online contact between children and unknown adults,” the commission said, adding that legislation, platform accountability and effective enforcement are essential for children’s online safety.

The NCRC noted the importance of striking an effective balance between children’s digital rights and their protection online.

The commission asserted that the issue of children’s online safety demands effective legal and institutional measures rather than mere policy. Advocates Muhammad Jalal Haider and Yahya Farid are representing the petitioner in the case.
