After talks between the NRL and Australian artist Tones And I, the grand final appeared set to take place without any pre-match entertainment.

However, on Friday it was revealed that an all-star ensemble of Australian musicians, led by Amy Shark, will lead a tribute to recently retired player Jai Arrow, who was diagnosed with MND earlier this year.

Shark will be joined by members from Newcastle favourites and Better hit-makers The Screaming Jets, plus rock groups Grinspoon, and Teen Jesus and the Jean Teasers.

Electronic duo Peking Duk revealed on Instagram on Sunday morning that despite rumours to the contrary, they would not be part of the performance.

Shark previously performed at the 2020 NRL grand final, and is set to perform a series of cover songs, including the Gerry and the Pacemakers' song and Liverpool FC anthem You'll Never Walk Alone.

Each musician's appearance fee is reportedly being donated to motor neurone disease causes.

World.title: Verstappen claims pole at Grand Prix in Malaysia
World.content:
Red Bull's Max Verstappen claimed his first pole position of the season at the Formula One Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia on Saturday, with Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton joining him on the front row.

It is the first time two great rivals have shared the front row of the grid since the Hungarian Grand Prix in 2023.

Verstappen's teammate, Isack Hadjar, was third fastest but will start eighth due to a grid penalty, with championship leader Kimi Antonelli in third alongside Ferrari's Charles Leclerc.

Oscar Piastri was pipped to sixth by his teammate Lando Norris, but will move up a position as a result of Hadjar's penalty to start sixth as McLaren locked out the third row of the grid.

George Russell, who so spectacularly won the last Grand Prix in Azerbaijan last week, will start seventh in what was an alarming performance for Mercedes, who came to Malaysia with a big upgrade package.

"It's very difficult to understand," Mercedes boss Toto Wolff told Sky Sports.

"We have been a little bit caught out on Friday with some car behaviour that we didn't see all year.

"But then you can say it's very hot, with the tarmac very different to all the tracks.

"[We] looked really good in the morning; we seemed to have, at least with Kimi [Antonelli], made a step in understanding. And then in qualifying, it was a little bit back to what we saw before — just no performance."

Verstappen was the last driver to win a Grand Prix in Malaysia in 2017, in what was his second career victory, before the race was taken off the calendar after the government said it could not justify the costs.

Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton will start from the front row of the grid together for the first time in three years. (Getty Images: Formula 1/Mark Sutton)

Nine years and four championships later, the Dutchman showed he was still the man to beat in Sepang with a time of 1 minute 35.130 seconds.

"It's fantastic, we've been trying for many Grands Prix to get more, sometimes a bit closer to the others. But to finally get it from where we started the season [it's] pretty incredible," said Verstappen as he eyes his first win of the season.

Hamilton, who also has one victory in Sepang, struggled with tyre degradation in practice sessions but the veteran Briton snatched second from Hadjar in the dying stages of the final qualifying session.

"It's so hot here, I keep saying it. But that's made it a massive challenge for the tyres, for the car, for the mechanics in the garage," Hamilton said.

"We made so many changes through all these practice sessions because the cars are sliding, these tyres are overheating. It was really, really hard to find a good balance. We made one last change going into qualifying and I think we hit the sweet spot."

Hadjar had exceeded his seasonal allowance for engines, which resulted in a five-place grid penalty.

"It's a bit unfortunate we take the penalty on a track that fast," Hadjar said.

"But you know, from P8, I'm confident we can go through the field and come back for a good result."

Reuters/ABC

World.title: De Minaur fights into quarterfinals in China
World.content:
Alex de Minaur has been pushed to the limit, before breaking the resistance of French qualifier Quentin Halys and advancing to his second consecutive China Open quarterfinal.

The Australian, who has had a seesawing second half of the year, lost the first set in Beijing on Saturday, before grinding his way back into the match.

After winning the first set 6-3, world number 50 Halys opened up a 5-3 lead in the second and was serving for the match, before de Minaur rallied to break back, then clinch a neck-and-neck tie break 7-5 to set up a decider.

The third set was another close affair, before de Minaur was able to break at 5-5 and secure a hard-fought 3-6 7-6 (5) 7-5 win in 2 hours 47 minutes.

Victory evened up their head-to-head record at 2-2 and put de Minaur into the quarters, where the world number 10 will play Andrey Rublev, currently ranked number 20 in the world, but a former top-10 player himself.

Rublev was also pushed to the limit before beating fellow Russian Roman Safiullin 6-2 3-6 6-4.

De Minaur will be looking to repeat or better last year's performance at the ATP 500 event, when he made the semifinals before losing to then world number 1 Jannik Sinner.

It has been an up-and-down year for de Minaur, who started 2026 off well by reaching the last eight at the Australian Open.

He continued that momentum into February, when he won the ATP 500 event in Rotterdam.

De Minaur followed that by reaching the French Open's third round and the fourth round at Wimbledon, before disappointingly bowing out in the second round of the US Open in September.

However, he bounced back impressively by steering Australia to victory over Poland in their Davis Cup clash in Brisbane, before beating in-from German Alexander Zverev at the Laver Cup in London.

Zverev, who has won two majors this year — at Roland Garros in June and Flushing Meadows in September — is top seed in Beijing and was scheduled to play China's Juncheng Shang later on Saturday.

AAP

World.title: David Fifita leads Australia in wild mismatch against PNG
World.content:
A rag-tag Australian side has outclassed Papua New Guinea 60-10 in the annual Prime Minister's XIII clash in Port Moresby.

The Australians scored 11 tries and exposed the PNG side's defensive frailties almost at will in what was the 20th men's Prime Minister's XIII match.

It was hardly a conventional game at the National Football Stadium on Saturday, with Australia switching on and off as players became accustomed to their makeshift position.

Ezra Mam spent time at fullback. Jock Madden appeared to be playing on an edge. Jamal Fogarty stood in the centres, and Josh Curran kicked a goal.

At one stage they had three regular hookers on the field.

In one piece of consistency, captain David Fifita started and finished the match as a devastating left centre.

Commentator Cooper Cronk mused it was coach Ben Teo's way of keeping the Aussies engaged after a long, hard season.

It was at times chaotic and they dropped the ball a lot, but it was fun. Less so for the PNG side, who were not just outclassed but also ill-disciplined, missing 47 tackles — 28 in the first half alone.

With the PNG Chiefs' arrival in the NRL fast approaching, it is clear the next level of local players are still a long way from that standard.

On a positive note, earlier on Saturday the Junior Kumuls scored a historic first win over the Australian Schoolboys, 18-10.

If Kangaroos coach Kevin Walters hasn't settled on his squad for this month's Rugby League World Cup, several players put their hands up.

Regular back-rower Fifita, who showed his class and power in the centres on Saturday, first appeared in the PM's XIII game seven years ago and looked destined for higher honours that never arrived. Maybe that time is approaching again.

Mam and fellow half Lachlan Galvin showed more than one glimpse of their brilliance, while hulking front-rower Tom Hazelton was one of the best players on the field.

For former NRL and current London Broncos coach Jason Demetriou, who will guide the PNG Kumuls at the World Cup, there was not a lot to love.

Sylvester Namo should be there, while uncapped centre Stanford Talita and fullback Sanny Wabo were dangerous at times and could find their way into Demetriou's squad.

In the women's game, Australia was also successful, dishing out a 66-6 thumping of their hosts.

The PNG women's Prime Minister's XIII scored a point for the first time in three years, but the Aussies still came out on top in a big way. (AAP: NRL Photos/Anthony Kourembanas)

PNG might have scored for the first time in three years, but Australia was a class above, crossing for 12 tries to one to rack up the biggest winning margin in the fixture's history.

While the standard of PNG's second-tier players has improved alongside the growth of the national women's competition, the Santos Cup, so too has that of the Australians.

Several showed they would not be out of place if called up to coach Jess Skinner's Jillaroos for this month's 2026 Rugby League World Cup.

Jada Taylor scored three tries and was almost impossible to handle at times, showing her versatility by playing on the wing, despite playing her club football at fullback.

Half Kasey Reh, centre Tahlia O'Brien, hooker Taneka Todhunter and back-rower Tayla Preston were others who impressed in what was effectively an audition in front of Skinner for a grander stage.

PNG Orchids coach Craig Sandercock, who this year guided Wests Tigers to their first NRLW finals series, would also have enjoyed the opportunity to see the next generation of PNG players.

There was no doubt they were outclassed, and they struggled for time with the ball, having just 37 per cent possession.

However, they had an 85 per cent completion rate and tried hard in defence, before tiring late in each half.

AAP

World.title: Saints hit rock bottom, Essendon, Suns, Port claim AFLW victories
World.content:
St Kilda have kicked just a single point, the club's lowest ever score in an AFLW match, as the Western Bulldogs scored a 30-point victory in Ballarat.

Incredibly, the Saints only managed the behind in the final 90 seconds of the game in a horror afternoon for the winless club.

The Bulldogs were barely better in tough conditions in Ballarat, with sideways rain and winds limiting the hosts to just three goals 13 on a day were accuracy in front of goal suffered.

Rylie Wilcox, Sarah Hartwig and Cleo Buttifant scored the goals for the Bulldogs, while Isabelle Pritchard (35 disposals, six clearances) was outstanding in the testing, cold conditions.

For the Saints, only Ashleigh Richards's point spared the cellar dwellers the ignominy of a bagel.

Earlier, star midfielder Madison Prespakis steered battling Essendon to an eight-point comeback victory over GWS for its first win of the season.

Essendon recorded its first win of the 2026 AFLW season. (Getty Images: AFL Photos/Mark Metcalfe)

The Giants got out to a game-high 25-point lead at the start of the third quarter and appeared on track for a second win of the season, before Prespakis kicked into overdrive and the Bombers lifted their pressure.

The star on-baller racked up 13 disposals, six contested possessions, three clearances and a goal in the third term to put Essendon on her back and inspire a terrific 6.7 (43) to 5.5 (35) comeback at Henson Park on Saturday afternoon.

"Genuinely just so proud of the resilience of the group," skipper Bonnie Toogood told Fox Sports.

"And it's been a challenging season, I suppose, and the persistence through adversity, particularly today.

"The first half wasn't what we were planning on, but to come out in the third like we did and just big moments by individuals — bloody inspiring."

The victory relieves some pressure on Bombers coach Natalie Wood and leaves St Kilda as the league's only winless team.

It was a devastating loss for Cam Bernasconi's Giants, who kicked five of the first six goals then only scored one point in a second half where they were completely overwhelmed by Essendon's manic pressure.

Madison Prespakis was sensational, with 13 disposals, six contested possessions, three clearances and a goal as the Bombers came from behind. (Getty Images: Jason McCawley)

Essendon had trailed by just four points at the final change when star forward Toogood gave the Bombers a massive rev-up at the huddle.

"I'm passionate and emotional all the time — it could be the Italian in me," Toogood said.

"They were on the back foot … I was like, 'We've got 'em — lean into that, we've got them, our football is working.'"

Essendon hit the front when it went from end to end and Daria Bannister tumbled home a long-range goal.

Then Emily Gough kicked a terrific checkside from a forward-50 stoppage that sealed victory.

Prespakis finished with a mammoth 35 disposals and five clearances, and she was well supported by Maddi Gay (21 disposals) and Georgia Gee (15), along with ruck Steph Wales (20 disposals, 14 hitouts, eight clearances).

Later, the Gold Coast Suns finally secured their first victory over the Brisbane Lions, winning a fiery Q-Clash by 20 points in Brisbane.

Havana Harris kicked two as the Suns won their first Q-Clash. (Getty Images: Albert Perez)

Meara Girvan may have cause for concern after pinning the arms of Cathy Svarc in a tackle during the first quarter, while Charlotte Mullins was penalised for high contact on Niamh McLaughlin later in the game.

The Lions led by two points at the final change but failed to kick another point as the Suns booted three in the final term to win 5.10 (40) to 3.2 (20).

Havana Harris kicked two for the Suns, who recorded their sixth win of the season to sit fourth on the ladder.

In Saturday's final fixture, Port Adelaide ended a four-match losing run by winning the Showdown against Adelaide in front of a record crowd of 5,441 fans at Alberton Oval.

Port Adelaide completed a second Showdown victory in a row at Alberton Oval. (Getty Images: Sarah Reed/AFL Photos)

The Power joined the Crows on 12 competition points thanks to a 5.6 (36) to 2.10 (22) victory.

Port (3-5) had five different goal kickers in the opening three quarters to open up a 34-7 advantage, but failed to hit the target in the fourth.

After going goalless for three terms, Caitlin Gould and Teah Charlton kicked straight for some respectability on the scoreboard for Adelaide (3-5).

AAP/ABC

World.title: FOMO and 4am wake-up call get Pallister in the ocean
World.content:
Is there anything Lani Pallister can't do?

On Friday night, Pallister wrapped up a hugely successful Australian short course championships with a fourth gold medal in the 800-metre freestyle to seal her spot in the 24-strong squad for the world championships.

Then, the 24-year-old rushed up to Queensland's Sunshine Coast to claim honours in the 1.2-kilometre Bluff to Bar ocean swim at Alexandra Headland on Saturday morning, after a 4am wake-up call.

"I'd get really bad FOMO [fear of missing out]," Pallister said when asked why she made the trip.

"It's important to give back … Alexandra Heads Surf Club helped make me the athlete I am today."

Lani Pallister won her third-straight Bluff to Bar race. (Supplied: Alexandra Headland Surf Lifesaving Club)

Pallister's dedication to her surf club cannot be doubted after she posted a story on her Instagram feed tagged at 4:38am to get her flight for an 11:20am race on the Sunshine Coast.

And the Paris Olympian made sure the early wake up was worth it, leading a stacked field from start to finish to claim a third-straight victory in the event.

Competing in a point-to-point ocean swim couldn't have been more different from the 125 tumble turns she completed in competition at the Sydney Olympic Park Aquatic Centre in the past four days.

Pallister competed in every freestyle event from 100m to 1,500m, winning gold in all but the 100m, where she finished second.

That ensured that she would be the headline act for the Dolphins squad named for the Beijing world championships from December 1-6.

The squad includes six debutants: Amelie Smith, Mark Nikolaev, Marcus Da Silva, Emily Jones, Cameron Bladen and Alex Quach.

Lani Pallister (left) and Jenna Forrester both had excellent championships. (Supplied: Swimming Australia/Delly Carr)

Head Dolphins coach Rohan Taylor noted Pallister's performance as a stand-out in Sydney, with Sam Short's clean sweep of the 400m, 800m and 1,500m freestyle and Jenna Forrester's four silvers and a gold also worthy of mention.

"Those three without a doubt have been stand-outs here," Taylor said.

"But also it's been great to see the likes of Amelie Smith and Marcus Da Silva come through the ranks and shift the dial.

"Also credit to Mark Nikolaev; it's a credit to his consistency and perseverance that he has earned his Dolphin number tonight.

"The international exposure in Beijing is an opportunity to come together and build towards LA 2028 and the meet presents a great opportunity for our younger swimmers to learn from established Dolphins."

Lani Pallister won the 200, 400, 800 and 1,500m freestyle events at the Australian short course championships. (Supplied: Swimming Australia/Delly Carr)

Speaking of experienced Dolphins, Cam McEvoy is also set to join the Aussie team in Beijing, despite not competing at the national championships this week.

World Aquatics is offering wildcard spots for the world championships to any to any swimmer who finishes on the podium of an individual final during the the World Cup series.

The 32-year-old long course world record holder duly set a new national short course record of 20.22 for the 50m freestyle to win gold on the opening night of the 2026 World Cup series in Baku, Azerbaijan, on Friday.

Pallister will now head for an altitude training camp in Flagstaff, USA, before the world championships, which represents her ninth Australian Dolphins selection.

"Off to altitude in a couple of weeks' time, and then just pretty much getting back into full training, knuckling down and targeting world champs," Pallister said during the short course titles.

"I didn't really anticipate fast swimming this week. I was actually pretty shocked with the 200 being plus 0.2, so [I'm] pretty happy."

Dolphins World Championships squad

Iona Anderson, Ben Armbruster, Cameron Bladen*, Brittany Castelluzzo, Josh Collett, Isaac Cooper, Marcus Da Silva*, Jenna Forrester, Max Giuliani, Emily Jones*, Tara Kinder, Mark Nikolaev*, Lani Pallister, Alexandria Perkins, William Petric, Alex Quach*, David Schlicht, Sam Short, Amelie Smith*, Flynn Southam, Stuart Swinburn, Matt Temple, Olivia Wunsch, Josh Yong.

*debut Dolphins squad

Tech.title: Capcom is preparing for a ‘future where we create games together with AI’
Tech.content:
is the Verge’s weekend editor. He’s covered the tech industry for over 18 years and knows a thing or two about synths.

Capcom’s Pragmata might be all about the horrors of AI, but in practice the studio doesn’t seem so down on the tech. During the Capcom Open Conference RE: 2026 programmer Satoshi Ishida gave a presentation with the mouthful of a title: “The Outlook and Future of the REX Project, Further Evolving the RE Engine for the Next Generation.” During the talk he laid out the challenges facing studios producing games at the scale of Resident Evil, which can make even simple tasks extremely time consuming. The solution Ishida said is “successfully integrating AI technology into development workflows.”

Capcom has said previously that it will not use AI-generated assets in its games, and instead would focus on using the tech to make development more efficient. Ishida’s comments seem to lineup, though definitely seem to leave the door open to more extensive use. He laid out a plan to turn RE Engine slowly, and incrementally, into an “AI-generation game engine” building towards a “a future where we create games together with AI,” according to IGN’s translation.
